First, get a container or cup that can hold the piping bag. Then take your piping bag and fold the top edge. Place it around your container and fill it with whatever you want. The reason we fold the edge is because that way if we get anything on the side, when we fold it up, it won't be at the very edge of the piping bag. And to get your filling to the bottom of the bag, all you have to do is grab and spin. And now your filling will be right at the bottom. with no air bubbles. Scrape everything together nice and neat. Now all you have to do is tie it off. Trim any excess bits. Perfectly filled piping bag top to bottom with no air bubbles. Won't explode or get on your hands even if you squeeze really hard. Super easy and clean and makes any job where you have to pipe that much easier.

hook: Fraternal twins genetic? Identical twins black magic.
template: (insert noun) (insert trait) (insert similar noun) (insert trait)
transcript: Fraternal twins genetic? Identical twins black magic. A little over two years ago, I gave birth to identical twins and I spent a lot of my time answering the same question. Do twins run in your family? I would like to take this moment on behalf of all parents of identical twins to explain the difference between fraternal twins and identical twins because they are in fact quite different. Fraternal twins are two separate eggs fertilized by two separate sperm. They are just regular siblings who happen to be born at the same time. Boy-girl twins, for instance, will always be fraternal. Fraternal twins and only fraternal twins are genetic. When people say they have twins in their family, this is what they are talking about. It is the gene that causes you to hyper ovulate, which means you are dropping multiple eggs at a time instead of just one. I don't know how to juggle, so I did that thing instead. Identical twins, on the other hand, are not genetic in any way. They can happen to anyone at any time. If you are a person who ovulates, it can happen to you too. They are not genetic, but rather a magic trick that your body plays on you. Here is how identical twins happen. Identical twins start out the exact same way all normal singleton pregnancies start. One sperm fertilizes one egg and then it becomes a zygote. The zygote is the thing that eventually becomes your baby. The way it becomes your baby is by multiplying its own cells. In the cell splitting process, it starts delegating. It says, "You cell over there. You be heart. You, you be eyes. You, you be another me." Unlike fraternal twins, which happen because of a gene that makes you drop hella eggs, bored. You know, it would be so funny if I cloned myself. My favorite fact about identical twins is that if a set of identical twins has children with another set of identical twins, their children, while legally cousins, are biologically full siblings. So to wrap it up, fraternal twins, regular siblings, identical twins, clones,

hook: Hi, my name is Tani, and this is my home, a school bus named Oliver. For five years, I lived and traveled in this bus, and together we've been over quite a few roads, all the way from Alaska down to Mexico.
template: Hi my name is (insert name) and this is my home
transcript: Hi, my name is Tani, and this is my home, a school bus named Oliver. For five years, I lived and traveled in this bus, and together we've been over quite a few roads, all the way from Alaska down to Mexico. Between travels, we had a home base in Montana, a small homestead we shared with family where we kept chickens and goats. Last year, we finally found a place that made us want to settle for good, so we packed up all those chickens and goats in a cargo van, and together with the bus, we caravan down to the Midwest where we purchased 10 acres of land in beautiful Missouri. This valley is our dream, an abundant forest teeming with mushrooms and wildlife and plants, with a pond and streams flowing through it and trees hundreds of years old. There were a few existing structures, but the last year was one of solid work building the foundations of our new homestead, mostly from scratch. First up were barns and fencing for all of our animals, which was good because we had quite a few new faces join us along the way over the last year. Then as spring arrived, we turned our attention to building a greenhouse and garden, creating compost and water systems, and an orchard to supply as much of our own food as we possibly can. We rounded out our first year by adding additional living space to Oliver in the form of a greenhouse-style bathhouse with a tub and shower supplied by the natural spring here, and an outdoor living area so we can continue to live outdoors as much as possible even though we aren't traveling anymore. We had a lot of amazing views out of these little bus windows during our travels, but it's a different kind of joy now when I look out in the mornings and realize that I, and Oliver, are finally home.

caption: Cherry chocolate fruit leather?? 🍒🍫 𝘿𝙚𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡𝙨: - 4 cups fresh or frozen cherries (pitted) - 1-2 tbsp maple syrup - Juice of 1/2 lemon (optional) - 1/3 cup chocolate chips - 1 tsp coconut oil 𝘿𝙞𝙧𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣𝙨: 1. hook: Day in the life of a selfish woman. I'm 32 years old with no desire to get married or have children and people often ask me if I met the right person would I change my mind?
template: Day in the life of a (insert adjective) person
transcript: Day in the life of a selfish woman. I'm 32 years old with no desire to get married or have children and people often ask me if I met the right person would I change my mind? The answer is no, I won't. Not wanting to be a mother has less to do with finding the right person than it does living a life free from avoidable stress. Although the thought of trying to co-parent with a man where I have to shoulder the majority of the emotional and physical labor sounds like a nightmare. No one is immune to life's challenges but at 32 I finally feel like I'm at a place where I can do what I want, when I want, without answering to anyone and it feels fucking awesome. Being a mother is really hard and I don't want to work hard. The idea of hard work has been glamorized by the institutions and people, mainly men, that benefit from a woman's labor the most. So I'll gladly take the easy way out if it means I don't have to stress about raising a child in a broken system that only rewards the smallest subset of the population if they fit neatly into a mold. And even then, what's really the reward? Most people don't have the privilege of self-actualization because they're forced to live paycheck to paycheck grinding away at unfulfilling jobs for just a few weeks of freedom a year if they're lucky. If I ever do choose to partner again, that person will share the sentiment that being a selfish woman isn't a flaw. It's a conscious rejection of the societal expectation that women must sacrifice themselves for others to be worthy or valuable and being selfish is a wonderful thing a woman can be.
author: chlobow_to
caption: Long live the selfish woman! 3 ingredient 🥞 recipe: Mash 1 ripe banana Wisk in 2 eggs Add 1/4 cup oats Cook on medium for 2ish minutes per side or until you can flip. Top with carmalized bananas (fry with butter and maple syrup) and drizzle with even more maple syrup 🍌💛

hook: This is what my morning looks like, fostering three medical pug puppies. First, I let everybody out and give them some yard time before heading back inside and getting all of their meds ready for the day.
template: This is what my morning looks like while (insert situation)
transcript: This is what my morning looks like, fostering three medical pug puppies. First, I let everybody out and give them some yard time before heading back inside and getting all of their meds ready for the day. These puppies were surrendered to our rescue after their mom died during labor and have had some health complications along the way. Right now, the two girls have some upper respiratory issues, so they're both getting some antibiotics every morning and night. After meds have been administered, it's time to eat. They all get puppy moose on licky mats since they're all so small. And they eat every four hours on the clock, so I have to do this multiple times a day. Easily their favorite part of the day. When they're eating, I get to work cleaning their puppy pen, but today was a deep, clean day. I do this about once a week, so I have to wash everything in there and make sure it's all scrubbed down. The sheer amount of laundry is the worst part about fostering puppies. I sweep and swiffer and deep clean the floor before laying down a new potty pad, and I reset up their heating pad and humidifier that helps with their pneumonia symptoms. Of course, the deep, clean day, fresh blankets are a must. They have a little nest area on their heating pad and then also their donut bed. I clean their water bowl in a fire, refill the tank, get everything back in there, and then get to work on taking care of myself, making myself breakfast. And then with the time I have left, I eat breakfast, hang out with the puppies, get them nice and tired before putting them back in their pen. By this point, it's about 8 a.m., and I can get going with the rest of my day once they're nice and tired.
author: bully.baloo
caption: A morning as a medical puppy foster! ❤️‍🩹 @bully.baloo Fostering these three babies has been so so much fun these past few weeks and l’ve loved every second of it! They have all been such amazing puppies and I’m so grateful l’ve been able to help them in their journey to finding their forever families. All three puppies are officially available for adoption through @caitiesfosterfamrescue! Adoption application is linked in my bio. 💕 Follow @bully.baloo for more adorable content! 🐾

hook: Six months into my home renovation, my worst nightmare became my reality. In March, 2023, I bought this charming house on the north side of Chicago with the best bones that needed a little extra love.

transcript: Six months into my home renovation, my worst nightmare became my reality. In March, 2023, I bought this charming house on the north side of Chicago with the best bones that needed a little extra love. My dad, who had spent his entire career in construction, graciously agreed to help me fix it up in his retirement. One of the home selling points was this empty attic that left potential to increase my square footage and equity in the house. In October, we got to work on bringing my vision to life. On my days off from work, dad worked at my speed so that I could help every step of the way. He taught me how to use a drill, a saw, measure, cut, and level. Not only was he my general contractor, he became the ultimate TikTok producer, recommending different shots and providing commentary while he filmed me. The days went by and we really started cruising on this project, especially once I figured out what the heck a 16th was. Our plans turned to realities and the space was really starting to take shape when our world was rocked. On March 4th, 2024, almost a year to the day that I bought my house, my dad was diagnosed with terminal brain cancer. We went from spending hours in the attic to spending hours in the hospital trying desperately to save him. Despite the best efforts of his medical team and all of the might he had, my dad passed from glioblastoma on June 23rd, 2024. On more than one day, I feared what would happen if one day my dad wasn't here to help me finish the house. But the thing about my dad is that from a young age, he always taught us that if he weren't here tomorrow, that he would want us to keep living our lives. I have received so much support since my dad's passing, which has helped me move on with my attic project. So many of our skilled friends and loved ones have donated their time to help me get the project back up and running. With their help, the electric and plumbing was installed,

author: joexfitness
caption: ⇩ Full Recipe 🥟 ⇩ Macros per 6 rolls: Protein: 53g Carbs: 23g Fat: 9g Calories: 375 Ingredients per 6 rolls: - 6 napa cabbage leaves - 1 second spray oil - 1/2 medium sized carrot - 2 green onion - 2 tsp minced garlic - 10oz red Argentine shrimp, raw - 1/2 tbsp sesame oil - 1 tbsp soy sauce - 1/2 tsp black pepper - 3 tbsp ponzu How to make it yourself: 1. Bring a pot of water to a boil 2. Add your nappa cabbage leaves into the boiling water until they start to become more bendy 3. Immediately transfer them to a bowl of cold water 4. Dice your green onions, cut you carrots into small pieces, and chop your shrimp onto small pieces 5. In a bowl, add in your green onions, carrots, and shrimp and mix in minced garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, and black pepper and mix 6. Lat your soft nappa cabbage leaves flat and add your shrimp veggie mix onto the leaves and roll them into small dumplings with the shrimp mix filling inside 7. In a pan on medium low heat coated with spray oil, add your “dumplings” and let them develop a brown sear on both sides and until the shrimp is cooked through 8. Once ready, transfer to your plate, pour your ponzu on top, and enjoy! 📩 Save this shrimp cabbage dumpling roll recipe to make for later and if you make it, post it and tag me in it! I’d love to see how you liked the recipe :)

hook: There are way too many green sauces in the world that sort of all look the same, but are they? If you mix together parsley, red wine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, chili, and oregano, you'll have a basic chimichurri from Argentina.
template: There are way too many (insert noun) in the world that sort of all look that same, but are they?
transcript: There are way too many green sauces in the world that sort of all look the same, but are they? If you mix together parsley, red wine vinegar, olive oil, garlic, chili, and oregano, you'll have a basic chimichurri from Argentina. If you replace the vinegar with lemon juice and swap out the chili and oregano for capers and anchovy, you'll have the Italian salsa verde, which is very different from the Mexican version. Change the parsley to cilantro, the lemon to lime, the olive oil for tomatillos, and the capers and anchovy for onion and jalapeno, and you'll have a basic version of the Mexican salsa verde. Now parsley, lemon zest, and garlic makes the Italian gremolata. Add cilantro, olive oil, cumin, and green chili, and it becomes the spicy green zug from Yemen. By replacing the green chili with paprika, it becomes similar to the Moroccan shramula. Swap out the parsley from it, add green chili, ginger, and cumin, and it becomes a basic green chutney from India. Now take all of that away. Basil, olive oil, garlic, pine nuts, and parmesan is the basis for an Italian pesto. By removing the parmesan and pine nuts, it then becomes a French pea stew. Now, if we combine every green sauce here together, we will create the swamp thing. It has a very generic green flavor. Pretty much just tastes like everything else here. I wonder why that is.

hook: 15 minutes ago, Poochie here was pulling around like crazy and had no engagement to me. If you want to teach your dog how to loose leash walk, here's how you do it in under five minutes.
transcript: 15 minutes ago, Poochie here was pulling around like crazy and had no engagement to me. If you want to teach your dog how to loose leash walk, here's how you do it in under five minutes. First, sudden U-turns. Pretty self-explanatory. You catch your dog when they're not paying attention to you and you walk the other way. It is not a pull towards you, it is a very clear pop. Your dog will start paying attention to you because they're walking one way and the train is going the other way, very clear. Secondly, you start with sudden stops. Sudden stops are great. Your dog's engaged with you and you'll start to see your dog pay attention to you. When they do pay attention to you, you heavily reinforce your dog and heavily praise the behavior. Last but not least, you want to walk around like a crazy person and I mean like a crazy person. This is sporadic walking. We change speed, change direction as well as mix in a lot of sudden stops and sudden U-turns. This should be a fun game for your dog and when they are paying attention to you, again, great things are happening. Your dog will start to think at all these environmental factors as nothing really important and start looking at you for absolutely everything. If you found this helpful, let me know in the comments below, hit the follow button. We'll see you in the next one.

hook: Let's start by mixing water and olive oil and I'm going to give it a good shake. What happens?
template: Let's start by mixing (insert noun) and (insert noun) and I am going to give it a good shake. What happens?
transcript: Let's start by mixing water and olive oil and I'm going to give it a good shake. What happens? The water and oil mix for a moment creating what's called a temporary suspension. Tiny droplets of oil dispersed in the water but you'll notice after just one minute they'll start to separate again. Now let's try the same thing but with pasta water and olive oil. And here's where the magic happens. The starchy pasta water acts as a bridge between the water and oil molecules allowing them to stay mixed together. This is how we create a smooth creamy sauce without separating. It's called an emulsion and it's a key technique when making sauces. Let's demonstrate this with a batch of spaghetti ayo e olio. Once the spaghetti is almost cooked I add it directly to the pan with olive oil and then pour in some of that starchy pasta water. When the olive oil and pasta water heat up together they start bubbling and this bubbling mimics the shaking of the test tube we saw earlier. The starch in the pasta water helps create an emulsion making the sauce creamy and smooth. This same emulsion technique is used when making salad dressings but instead of pasta water I'm using ingredients like Dijon mustard or honey the binder.
author: michaeltchao
caption: ESSENTIAL SAUCE TECHNIQUE Ever wonder why some sauces come out silky smooth, while others separate? It all comes down to emulsions! In this video, we see how pasta water works its magic in a classic aglio e olio sauce. The starch from the water acts as a natural emulsifier, binding the olive oil and water together into a perfect, creamy sauce. And here’s the cool part: this same trick applies when making salad dressings! Whether it’s Dijon mustard or honey, these ingredients act as emulsifiers to keep your oil and vinegar mixed. Also, this is why it’s better to mix dressings BEFORE adding salad ingredients

transcript: One day, you're gonna get dumped. Not by your boyfriend, not by your girlfriend, or your fiance, or your spouse. By your best friend. You know, the one that you talk to or cry with, when your boyfriend cheats on you, when your parents kick you out of your house. The one who like psychically knows to text you at that exact moment with, hey, the one you can be a complete slob around, eat an entire chocolate cake with. That person's gonna dump you one day. And you won't be ready for it, 'cause you can't be ready for it. So what you're gonna end up doing is you'll play the final scenes of your friendship over and over and over. again. You'll ask yourself, like, maybe if I just did this, or maybe if I didn't do that, we'd still be friends. You'll start to ask yourself, well, maybe I don't even deserve any friends. Maybe it's not that I'm just a bad friend. Maybe it's that I'm a bad person. Because if the one person who knows you better than anyone else in the entire world determines that you're not good enough for them, then maybe you're not good enough, period. But here's the thing, babe, and I need you to listen, 'cause this one's gonna be really hard. It's them. It's not you. So what you're gonna do is get off that hamster wheel right now. And you're gonna shut down all those little voices that are telling you that you're not good enough, because you are good enough for me. And more importantly, you're good enough for you. Don't worry, you're not gonna die alone. I know it feels that way, because you've got me. Now, blah, blah, blah.

caption: Friend breakups are hard. They entail a totally different kind of hurt that romantic breakups—almost like it’s a different part of your heart that’s being broken. Although they do look delicious like Lion King worthy, we're about to witness their beautiful transformation. I got some coconut fiber and got ready to place them right inside. They turn into hawk moths, so not exactly from the butterfly family, but they are from the same order and that they both grow scaled wings. And they have a relatively short lifespan as moths of about two to three weeks. It can take 30 to 50 days to transform from an egg to an adult, though. And you can't let them loose because they're an invasive species. It's more about just my own desire to learn about animal species that I'm unfamiliar with and hopefully educate others on the beauty that surrounds their lifecycle. They eat this chow and tomatoes, but they become toxic when they eat tomatoes. Not like dogs and cats. Don't worry. I was joking, but don't forget to follow if you want to witness what happens when they go into the cocoon stage. It's going to happen in the next few days with our big one because it's already changing color from bluey to yellow. I'm so excited. Oh my God.

hook: I didn't realize how bad I lost myself. I was showing up, doing everything right, checking the boxes, being disciplined.
template: I didn't realize how bad I lost myself
transcript: I didn't realize how bad I lost myself. I was showing up, doing everything right, checking the boxes, being disciplined. But I wasn't present. I was living in autopilot. Comfortable, but completely unaligned. I allowed people and patterns into my life that didn't reflect the woman I wanted to become. I kept peace at the cost of my own. And the worst part, I didn't even notice it was happening. I was tired, dealing with acne, bloated, burnt out. No matter what I did, I felt like my body was fighting me. But it hit me. I can't grind my way into change. I can't restrict or push my way into alignment. Because the truth was, I was still holding onto a version of me who wanted to stay stuck. Everything shifted the moment I stopped performing and started listening. And for the first time in a long time, I chose me. I burned the habits, the stories, the people pleasing. And piece by piece, I came home to myself. And I became a woman I'm proud of. Not because she's perfect, but because she's real. So if you're in a place where you've lost sight of who you are, just know that you don't have to stay there. You're not broken. You're not behind. You're just waiting to remember who you are. And when you're ready, you can burn what's no longer yours. And finally, become her.
author: meagnunez
caption: There’s a moment in every woman’s life where she realizes… she’s been performing. Performing strength. Performing discipline. Performing a version of herself she’s outgrown. And behind the routine, the hustle, the perfection is a woman who feels disconnected. Tired. Unseen. And unsure why she’s doing everything “right” but still doesn’t feel like her. That was me. Until I stopped performing… and started listening. Until I stopped chasing change… and started releasing what was never mine to carry. This isn’t about a glow-up. This is about coming home to yourself. Burn to Become is not just a story. It’s a remembrance. It’s a rebirth. It’s the moment you choose you — fully, finally, and without apology. If this touched something in you… It’s because the next version of you is waiting. And she’s ready to rise. Ready to stop burning out and finally become who you were made to be? And then this is where I learned how to snowboard. Now I wasn't very good at the start but I slowly got better. After my visa extension got rejected I ended up in immigration. It was during COVID I didn't want to go home so I booked a one-way ticket to Hawaii. I had no place to stay and very little money but I got lucky and got a job in a hostel. I stayed in Hawaii for nine months and loved every second of it. And then after the nine months I'd saved up enough money to do it all over again. Ended my time in Honduras before getting a flight to the US. Drove the whole way across the US from Florida to the Pacific Northwest. I then went back to Hawaii, got another job in a hostel. Saved up some more money and then moved to South Africa. I stayed in South Africa for three months. I don't actually have a sleeping bag. This is where we got a car and started a road trip of Southern Africa. Again we surfed the whole way up from South Africa to Mozambique. Drove the whole way to Victoria Falls in Babué. Wild camped in the saltpans in Botswana. Before reaching the midi and circling back to South Africa. I started organizing surf camps in Jefferies Bay. Over the next couple of months I ran three. In between the camps I went and explored Mauritius and also went and got food poisoning in Madagascar. I then ran an untrained marathon for my friend's NGO. They nearly killed me but we were raised 9,000 euro. The plan next was to head home for a while. So we bought a car in South Africa and currently driving home to Ireland. I wanted something that was aesthetically pleasing and provided both ambient and directional light, so I ripped down a bunch of these thin strips of maple. I cut the ends at a compound angle and glued all the pieces up to form the layers of the lampshade. Next, I needed to make some sort of arm for the lampshade to hang from, which would also conceal the electrical wiring. This lamp was going to slide smoothly back and forth on the wall mounted rail, it would need some bearings to reduce the friction. After installing these two bearings to alleviate the downward friction, I added more vertically that would allow it to slot into the wall mounted track. And after quite a bit of trial and error, I got it to work. I glued in these clear plastic rods to act as spacers so that light could shine in between the layers of the lamp, and then I connected the lamp to the arm with this brass bolt. In order for this whole idea to work, I needed a pulley system with a rope that pulls the lamp back and forth, so I installed more bearings at each end of this track that I built. The final step was soldering everything together, and it was time to install the track on the wall. To attach the lamp assembly to the pulley, I just wrapped the cord around the vertical bearing assembly. The lamp plugs directly into the nightstand that I built, which has an integrated dimmer knob, and I can move the lamp easily to either end of the track just by pulling the rope.

Pretty good, but certainly nothing special, and I think we can do better. If you replace the egg with a buttermilk marinade, instead of a regular flour, you season flour, you'll have something to pin to a southern style fried chicken. Juicier and more tender from the buttermilk, and with an irresistibly flavorful skin from all the seasonings. If you replace the buttermilk with a soy marinade, and then replace the flour with potato starch, you'll have something similar to a Japanese-style karaage, often served with kyūpimeo and lemon. The soy marinade gives it that signature tang, the potato starch reduces moisture, giving it more crunch. If you replace the soy marinade with a wet batter, and instead of potato starch used corn starch, you'll end up with something similar to a Korean-style fried chicken. Blaze it up, and you'll have one of the most delicious bites in existence. The wet batter has air bubbles, which are then trapped by a layer of corn starch, which in tandem creates a crispy yet light and airy texture. Now all that yapping aside, time to address the real question. What happens if you combine every single method here mentioned together? So onions are actually a cold resistant crop. So when it's exposed to low temperatures and moisture, the starches will convert to simple sugars and then this will attract mold formation. So we've all done it. We've cut an onion and put the unused portion in the fridge. In fact, what happens is when you put it in the fridge, it absorbs all the bacteria and it forms mold. In Ayurveda, an ancient remedy is actually when someone is sick, we cut an onion and put it in the fridge and put it in a corner of the room so it can actually absorb and attract all those pathogens. Number three is ginger. This is not meant to be exposed to the cold or to moisture. Once you put ginger in the fridge, it forms mold and this has been linked to liver and kidney failure. So always keep at room temperature. The fourth one, this probably is confusing because you've seen a lot of recent reports on why you should refrigerate this, but it's rice. Never refrigerate rice. And if you do, never more than 24 hours. This is one of the highest mold forming foods. Now there's a lot of talk about if you refrigerate right after you cook it, you can increase the resistant starch and this is great for your cholesterol and blood sugar. That may be so, but it's not worth the risk of getting mold and it can form a serious bacteria which causes food poisoning and even can lead to death. So those are the four foods that you should never refrigerate.

hook: When making brownies, the mixing method is just as important as the ingredients. The creaming method starts by mixing sugar and butter together until fluffy and finishes with the eggs and dry ingredients.
template: When making (insert noun) the (insert noun) is just as important as the (insert noun)
transcript: When making brownies, the mixing method is just as important as the ingredients. The creaming method starts by mixing sugar and butter together until fluffy and finishes with the eggs and dry ingredients. Because of all the air incorporated in the first step, these brownies are the cakiest, and since the cocoa powder is added at the end, the cocoa flavor is the most intense. The sponge method, on the other hand, starts by mixing eggs and sugar together. The cocoa is mixed with butter and then added before finishing with the flour. This time, because the sugar has had time to dissolve in the eggs, the brownies have a shiny, crackly top. The side is much fudgier, and because the cocoa bloomed in the hot butter, the chocolate flavor is smoother. Finally, in the wet and dry method, the cocoa and all the wet ingredients are mixed together before adding the dry. hook: Mom, the poor boys, this is how I treat being a stay-at-home mom like a job. If you do the math, stay-at-home parents work roughly 90 plus hours a week and would get paid at least $180,000 based on the task they do, which is why these are the six ways I treat being a stay-at-home mom like a job.
template: Mom/Dad of # of kids, here is how I treat being a mom/dad as a job
transcript: Mom, the poor boys, this is how I treat being a stay-at-home mom like a job. If you do the math, stay-at-home parents work roughly 90 plus hours a week and would get paid at least $180,000 based on the task they do, which is why these are the six ways I treat being a stay-at-home mom like a job. One, I identify a start time and an end time to my day. I wake up at 5.15 a.m. every day, but I'm not mom until 7 a.m. and my kids are generally respectful of this. They also know that by 8 p.m. my husband and I are generally off the clock. Two, I wake up before I clock in as mom. I wake up almost two hours before my kids to take care of the things that make me a better me before I go to work as mom. This includes mental exercises and a workout. You wouldn't show up to a job in distress. It's important I don't show up as mom this way either. Three, before I start work as mom, I get myself ready for the job. Why do I get myself ready for the day? Simply put, I have respect for the work that I do and dressing nice makes me more energetic and productive. Plus, I want my kids to know that looking nice matters. Four, I stay organized with schedules and I hold family meetings. Just like any other high-performing job, mommy requires organization scheduling and meetings, which is why we hold a meeting every Sunday where I organize our weekly schedules and meal plans. Five, I take breaks. Being a parent is demanding and if you don't find ways to take breaks, you will burn out, which leads me to. Six, I understand the importance of outsourcing as a mom. I understand that outsourcing can be a privilege and also a mom's greatest fear, but the best businesses find ways to hand off things that lighten the load when possible. Every other week, we outsource house cleaning to our incredible housekeeper, Miss Anna. And that's how I treat being a stay-at-home mom like a job.
author: brookeraybould
caption: Being a mom is more of a calling than a job; it’s more of an art than a science. But it doesn’t mean that your calling, or your art, shouldn’t be treated as a job, especially if you take it seriously. 👉🏻First, comment the word “JOB” and I will send you a 24-page PDF guide that outlines why and how I do this (free!) for a limited time. Think of an artist. Their mission is to create beautiful art. But, to make a living, they need to sell their art. They probably need a marketing strategy, website, business banking account, accounting, and so on. Suddenly, their “art” starts to run itself like a business. Because it is. It’s the same (in my opinion) as being a mom. You become a mom and your kids are not a job; they are your art; your beautiful creation. But the things that surround motherhood are, in fact, a job. And like a job, these elements require organization, boundaries, outsourcing, and more to thrive. As someone who struggled in the early years of motherhood and as someone with a master’s in business, about five years and three babies in as a mom, I realized I needed more structure in motherhood. I wanted to do this mom thing strategically - in a way that would honor my craft, so I could be ALL IN without burning out. Once I identified the surrounding roles of motherhood as a “job”, I could then start fine-tuning my organizational approach to motherhood. I created rhythms, structure, flow, benchmarks, frameworks. Improvement started happening and as a high-achieving female in a stay-at-home mom role, I thrived. Yes, I understand many people are not wired the way I am!! But so many ARE wired like I am. This message is for you. You need structure, goals, and a healthy challenge. There’s nothing wrong with you! The minute you embrace who you are; the minute your joy in motherhood will exponentially take off. You’re capable and you’ve got this! 🙌🏻♥️

It's honestly one of the most remarkable things I've ever seen and I always knew it was possible. What I didn't see coming however is the reason that I've actually made this choice. Pain. transcript: These are the 3 most common mistakes I see people making when making chocolate covered strawberries. So you can avoid them and get the same quality chocolate covered strawberries as you would in a store. The first mistake I see people making is that they don't acid wash their strawberries. The strawberries might look perfect, but they're full of mold spores all the way around. In order to kill those mold spores, rinse them in a bath of 1 cup water and 1 cup white vinegar for about 15 minutes. This will prevent your strawberries from going mushy and gooey after they're dipped in the chocolate. The second mistake I see people making is that they don't properly dry their strawberries. The third mistake I see people making is that they don't thin out their chocolate. There's nothing worse than having a chocolate covered strawberry you bite into it and it's this thick shell of chocolate. You want it to be nice, thin, and crispy. Now it's going to melt a little bit more evenly and it's going to be a thinner consistency which is better for dipping your strawberries.

Understanding the GLUTES The glutes consist of three muscles: Gluteus Maximus – The largest muscle, responsible for hip extension, external rotation, and some abduction. Gluteus Medius & Minimus – Located on the upper and outer side of the glutes, these muscles are crucial for hip abduction and stabilization. While we can’t completely isolate one specific part of the glutes, we can bias different regions through strategic exercise selection and loading positions. Upper glutes + side glutes: Best targeted by focusing on loading in a shortened position (peak contraction). Lower glutes: Best targeted by exercises that load them in a lengthened position (deep stretch). When you lift weights, this causes damage and also the addition of new myofibers, which are separate processes. Protein provides the building blocks for repair and new growth, but you also need enough recovery time. This is around 48 hours before you should target the same muscle group again. author: tombaileypt
caption: What happens to MUSCLES when you lift weights? 💪🏼 Read 👇🏼 This is a post about the RECOVERY process, NOT what causes muscle growth 👀 In the video I mention that there are 2 SEPARATE processes… Muscle growth and the process of muscle repair after damage are SEPARATE processes, although they both require an increase in muscle protein synthesis rates 📈 To signal muscle GROWTH, we need high amounts of mechanical tension, this triggers the addition of new myofibrils within muscle fibres 💪🏼 However, when we lift weights, based on many factors such a rep ranges, total volume, stretch position exercises, eccentrics etc… this can cause DAMAGE 💢 Damage is NOT the driver of muscle growth, and is simply a byproduct of lifting - which ideally, we want to minimise 📉 P.S. the damage is not muscles ‘tearing’ - it is better described as structural disruptions or stress to muscle fibres and associated cellular structures (a muscle tear would be an injury) 😢 Muscle protein synthesis is the SAME pathway for both muscle growth (from the mechanical tension stimulus) and muscle recovery (to repair any muscle damage) 🛜 BUT - they’re separate processes, and purposefully seeking out ‘damaging’ exercises or training methods may hinder your muscle hypertrophic response! 💪🏼 Workouts themselves aren’t ‘building muscle’ they are creating the DEMAND for growth 📈 The demand MUST be met with adequate SUPPLY of protein & recovery time to elicit a successful growth response ⚖️ I didn’t think I needed to specify this, but the video is for dramatic illustration purposes ONLY - your muscles don’t actually turn into shredded beef LMAO😂 Hope this clears things up! 😎🤝

Keeping the flavor simple with a peanut butter and jelly, I love using the back of a spoon to make this pretty wave pattern and topping with pistachios for added crunch. Next is the classic avocado toast with a sunny side up big and scallion. And I love enjoying this at home while remembering someone is paying $20 at a gentrified neighborhood cafe for it. Next, if you take a whole lot of a piece of bread, coat both sides with mayonnaise or butter before cracking an egg and cooking on medium-high heat until golden brown, you'll be well on your way to making a toad and a hole, or one of the other 100 names that's known to you. Next, moving on to custard toast, starting by making a simple batter of egg, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon, soaking a thick slice of challah brioche or any stale bread for maximum absorption, and cooking that over medium heat in some butter until golden brown. Can't go wrong with French toast, but what if instead we put the custard in the center of the toast? This time, a quick custard of egg, Greek yogurt, and maple syrup goes into a crusty divot in the middle of a piece of soft bread. Then just air fry it 350 until set and starting to caramelize before adding on any toppings. And if you want to make something fancy that takes zero effort, these last drove for you. If you don't have a piping bag, a Ziploc bag with the end for this ricotta and lemon combination, that's unbelievably good. And for a dairy-free version that tastes way better than some of its parts, blend tofu, olive oil, and beets together. Happy toasting!
author: reidstestkitchen
caption: Every way to make toast Recipes: 1. Classic - butter, honey, flaky salt 2. PB&J - use the back of a spoon to make scalloped waves on the toast in an alternating pattern and top with pistachio pieces and flaky salt 3. Avocado Toast - for the perfect sunny-side-up egg, cook over medium-low heat and cover for 30s to 1 minute to fully cook the white 4. Toad-In-A-Hole - Preheat pan over medium-high. Take a hole out of the center of a piece of bread and spread mayonnaise or butter on each side. Add to pan and crack an egg in the middle. Cook on the first side until golden brown, then just for 30s-1 minute on the second side until crisped up but the yolk still feels runny to the touch 5. Classic French Toast - Custard of 1 egg, 1/4 cup milk, splash of vanilla and 1/4 tsp cinnamon. Soak challah, brioche, or stale bread for best soaking potential. Cook over medium-low in butter or a neutral oil like avocado 6. Custard Toast - Preheat air fryer to 350F/180C. Custard of 1 egg, 2 tbsp greek yogurt, and 1 tbsp maple syrup or honey mixed well goes into a divot made with a spoon in the middle of a piece of soft bread. Air fry until custard is set and starting to caramelize on the edges. Top with berries and a drizzle of maple syrup or honey 7. Ricotta Toast - Add ricotta to a piping bag or ziploc with the end snipped off. Pipe onto toast before topping with lemon zest and honey 8. Whipped Tofu Toast - Blend 1 block of firm tofu, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 2 cooked beets together with salt and pepper to taste. Pipe onto toast, topping with scallions and fresh cracked black pepper

hook: Have you ever noticed that some cables feel ridiculously light in your hands and others feel ridiculously heavy? Why is that?
template: Have you ever noticed that some (insert noun) feel (insert description) while others feel (insert description)
transcript: Have you ever noticed that some cables feel ridiculously light in your hands and others feel ridiculously heavy? Why is that? Imagine you're lifting 100 pounds on a cable stack in three different scenarios. In scenario A, only one cable directly attaches to the weight stack. In scenario B, a pulley with two cables coming off of it attaches to the weight stack. And in scenario C, two pulleys with four total cables attached to the weight stack. In scenario A, where there's a direct attachment and you are lifting 100 pounds. In scenario B, you're actually only lifting 50 pounds because the weight gets distributed through two different cables. So what's in your hand ends up being only half the weight on the stack. And in scenario C, because there are four cables and the weight is distributed through four different places, you're only lifting a quarter of the load. So it makes sense that cables with more pulleys are lighter, right? Wrong. Most companies already account for this. So what the weight stack says is actually the force that's going through the handle, but cable sacks do feel lighter and heavier. So what actually makes the difference here? It's really only in how much or how little the weight stack moves. So watch what happens when I move the A version of the stack, the one with the direct attachment. You'll notice that it moves 100% of the distance that my hand moves when I move the cable. Now watch what happens when I move the B stack, the one with one single pulley. You'll notice that it actually only moves 50% of the total distance that my hand is moving. Now guess what happens to the C stack. It now only moves 25% of the distance. So what the hell does this actually do and why does it matter? Well, imagine you have three cars, each of which represents each of the stacks. Car A drives one mile, car B drives half a mile, and car C only drives a quarter of a mile. Now imagine each car has the same amount of time, let's say 30 seconds to travel their distance. Car A needs to travel roughly a hundred miles an hour to travel a mile in 30 seconds. Car B though only needs to travel at 60 miles per hour and car C only needs to travel at 30 miles per hour. So the farther the car moves in the same amount of time, the faster it needs to drive. It's pretty obvious. So when you move a weight stack more in the same exact amount of time, the weight stack itself needs to travel faster, meaning that you pulling on the handle need to generate higher force. So what's the simple takeaway? Well, stacks that move more in the same amount of time feel heavier and stacks that move less feel lighter. And I actually do think that this is important for your gains because oftentimes the stacks that move less feel a lot smoother. And when they feel a lot smoother, they actually feel typically better on people's joints. So if you don't need a ton of load for an exercise and you have the option to choose between different cable stacks, I would generally choose the one that moves a smaller distance because it'll probably feel smoother. And in the long run, it may end up feeling a bit better on your joints, which is obviously super, super important for growing muscle.

hook: One of the best ways to save money while cooking. Well, one starts with cutting foods at home.
template: Best ways to save money while (insert action)
transcript: One of the best ways to save money while cooking. Well, one starts with cutting foods at home. Take pineapple. A small pack of pre-cut pineapple will cost twice as much as a whole one. But cut it up in about 10 minutes and you'll not only get double the weight of the pre-cut, but at half the price. That's not a half bad deal. As another example, this pre-cut chicken breast cost me more than this entire chicken. But again, after taking about 10 minutes to break it down into your thighs, drumsticks, wings and breasts, I get the same chicken breast weight as the pre-cut, but then drums, thighs and wings that are essentially free in comparison. Not only that, but you have a carcass to freeze for later, which brings me on to my next point. Each time you cook, keep a bolt of hand to toss them into and start accumulating them in a bag in the freezer. And when your collection's looking sizable, defrost the scraps and carcasses if you have them and begin with roasting them with oil for a half an hour to color. Then adding your brown greens and optional bones into a stock pot, adding water and aromatics like bay leaves and pepper, then leaving it to simmer for three to four hours, then straining once finished. After all that, you're left with a beautiful stock perfect for gravies, broths, soups, braises, sauces and much more. All from things that would have otherwise been chucked.

hook: build an app with me with AI while flying to New York. Let me be honest, I've never built an iOS app before, despite majoring in CS.
template: Build a (insert noun) with me while I (insert action)
transcript: build an app with me with AI while flying to New York. Let me be honest, I've never built an iOS app before, despite majoring in CS. So the first thing I did was watching this three hour long YouTube tutorial on the basics of Xcode and Swift. Because even with AI, I do not have an idea of what's going on. So what am I building? The app is essentially a time zone converter. To simplify meeting scheduling, it outputs a shareable message. The inspiration was from my own struggle when I was in China, trying to plan meetings with teammates across three, four different time zones. But when I started the project, I quickly realized it was way more complicated than the tutorial. So I waited until I had internet after my layover in Seoul to prompt GPT for some help. The code has some errors, and before I could debug, I lost internet. So I took a nap and really locked in during my six hour layover in Hawaii. This time I switched to cursor, which if you don't know, is a very powerful AI code editor. I use their Composer feature, which not only generates code, but allows simultaneous multi-file editing. It basically wrote the whole app. With only a few rounds of debugging, the app was up and running. You can select your time zone, your teammates' time zone, and a future meeting time. It then generates a message you can share instantly. I had some UI adjustments and generated a logo with Mid-Journey. Before I even boarded my last flight, I had a functional app. It was insane. If you ever had an app idea but didn't think you were technical enough, come and build and I'll share the exact prompt template I used and follow to see what I build next.

hook: When I was growing up, one card game that I played all of the time with my mom was speed. And if you've never played before or if you need a refresher, shuffle your favorite deck and I'll teach you right now.
template: When I was growing up one (insert noun) I always (insert verb) with my (insert person) was (insert noun)
transcript: When I was growing up, one card game that I played all of the time with my mom was speed. And if you've never played before or if you need a refresher, shuffle your favorite deck and I'll teach you right now. In speed, you'll go head to head competing to be the first player to get rid of all of your cards. To the center, deal out a stack of five cards followed by two single cards and then a second stack of five cards. The rest of the deck is dealt out evenly between you and your opponent. Draw a hand of five cards from your personal deck and then you're ready to play. Simultaneously, you and your opponent will flip over those two cards in the center. of the table. This begins the game. You both will play at the same time, discarding cards from your hand into these center piles. To discard a card, it must be one rank higher or lower than the top card of the pile you're playing onto. This means that you can only discard a five on top of a four or a six. Now the rank order loops, so you can play an ace on a king or on a two. You can only ever play one card at a time though. You can't put down a run of cards at once. Your hand is limited to five cards, but once you've played a card, you can draw new cards from the top of your deck to bring your hand back up to five. If during the game you are ever locked out and neither you nor your opponent has a play, you'll each draw the top card off of your stack of five and place them into the center piles. If you still can't play, just do it again. If you ever run out of moves and you don't have any cards left in the stacks, just flip over the center piles and keep going. You'll do all of this as quickly as you can, rushing to play all of your cards before your opponent. The first player to discard all of their cards, shouts speed and wins.

caption: Speed Quick Rules 💨 ⬇️ Speed is a fun game for two players. All you need is one standard deck of cards! Make sure to follow so you don’t miss any future card game tutorials, and binge watch the ones you’ve missed here 👉 Need a new deck? Comment CARDS and I’ll send you a DM with a link to all my favorite ones, including this beautiful floral set from @riflepaperco . How to play Speed: Goal: Be the first to get rid of all your cards. Setup: Deal each player 20 cards: 5 cards in hand + 15 in a face-down draw pile. Place two face-down 5-card side stacks in the center. Place two single cards face down between them How to Play: Play cards one at a time onto either play pile—must be 1 rank higher or lower (e.g., 6 on 5 or 7). No turns—play as fast as you can. Refill your hand up to 5 cards from your draw pile anytime. Stuck? Flip a new card from each side stack to refresh the center piles. If side stacks are gone, reshuffle center piles to restart. 🏆 Win: First to play all cards from hand and draw pile wins      @rathskellers

caption: I devoured these in 3 days lol 𝘿𝙚𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡𝙨: Oatmeal Base: - 2 cups rolled oats - 1/2 cup almond or peanut butter - 1/4 cup honey or maple syrup - 1 tsp vanilla extract - Pinch of salt Chocolate Topping: - 1/2 cup dark chocolate chips (can use more or less) - 1/2 tsp coconut oil 𝘿𝙞𝙧𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣𝙨: 1. caption: COMMON BULGARIAN SPLIT SQUAT MISTAKES ❌ There are so many tips and cues when it comes to the Bulgarian split squat, but here are a few key ones I see a lot that can really mess with your form: 1️⃣ Overextending the back leg – Make sure your back leg is at a comfortable angle, not too far behind you. This helps with balance and prevents unnecessary strain. 2️⃣ Not slightly leaning forward – A slight forward lean in the torso helps target the glutes and hamstrings more effectively. Stay upright, but don’t lock your body in place. 3️⃣ Knee collapsing inward – Keep that knee tracking over your toes! If it caves in, it puts a lot of stress on the joint and throws off your alignment. 4️⃣ Bouncing at the bottom – Control the movement! Don’t let gravity take over. hook: Ever since I was little my mom made it very clear to me that she was embarrassed about certain aspects of our culture. She would never let me bring kimchi to school after a certain point and when non-korean friends came over after school she would always apologize in advance for the smell.
template: Ever since I was (insert adjective) my (insert person) made it very clear to me that he/she was (insert adjective) about certain aspects of (insert noun)
transcript: Ever since I was little my mom made it very clear to me that she was embarrassed about certain aspects of our culture. She would never let me bring kimchi to school after a certain point and when non-korean friends came over after school she would always apologize in advance for the smell. Yesterday I went to my mom's house to make a kimchi making video and my mom kept insisting that we sauce the kimchi on a table instead of the floor even though in all my memory it's always been done on the floor. Once again my mom was worried about appearances and I thought she was just being overly self-conscious. She had a picture of us doing our kimchi squat on twitter and then somebody replied with this. And I was furious. Not for me but for my mom. My 72 year old mom who spent the last half of her life assimilating into this country still needs to be afraid of this. That she still needs to be self-conscious about her culture. That she's still being told that the white way is the only right way. For the record I'm done apologizing and so is my mom.
author: thekoreanvegan
caption: My mother was about as “in your face” as she could be in our home and my father has been politically active since he was a teenager. I cannot begin to describe how grateful I am for their indirect tutelage, the values they instilled in me, and the tools they gave me to voice my opposition to the things I view as wrong. My parents are still immigrants, though. And often times, the language and cultural barriers, as well as the insecurity that inheres to assimilation, disguise micro-aggression so well, it becomes susceptible to internalization. This breaks my heart. And makes me so angry. Because my parents don’t deserve that. . Some ppl will watch this and say, what’s the big deal? Some ppl don’t want their kimchi prepared on the floor. But that misses the point. That precise attitude—one that my mother predicted—is what will eradicate traditional practices from cultural cuisine. Why do we make kimchi on the floor? Because it’s meant to be a communal activity. Kimchi making day is a full day affair, with women from not just your entire family but the entire village gathering together to salt and sauce the cabbage. You need to get all up in there, sometimes elbow deep, and the most efficient way to do that with so many ppl is to put it on a level surface that is within arms reach of several, with sufficient leverage to do so for long periods of time (hence, the “kimchi squat”). I am happy to explain this to the curious, but saddened to explain it to the arrogant and condescending, those who think that their way—the way of the dominant culture—is the ONLY right way. . I didn’t post this to my Insta (it’s been on my TikTok for awhile), because it’s been a bit tiring dealing with the amount of times I’ve been told “you’re making a bit deal out of nothing,” “ewwww I wouldn’t want to eat off your floor [news flash there’s a freaking bowl],” or, my personal favorite “you’re racist.” But gaslighting comes with the territory and I need to learn how to cope with it. . The recipe link for this amazing vegan pop “chicken” is in my bio. Or here: https://thekoreanvegan.com/ricepop-ricepaper-tofu/ Enjoy. It’s a winner for sure

hook: Did you know you only need three ingredients to make cheese? I'm going to show you how to do it.
template: Did you know you only need # of ingredients to make (insert noun)
transcript: Did you know you only need three ingredients to make cheese? I'm going to show you how to do it. The first thing you need to make cheese is whole milk. I personally like to use a raw milk that is not homogenized and it's not ultra pasteurized. I heat my milk on medium until the temperature reaches about 100 degrees. The next ingredient is plain yogurt. This will provide the bacteria needed to ferment the milk. I added about three tablespoons of yogurt to a bowl and added a bit of milk to it to thin it out. Next, I took my pot of milk off the heat and added that yogurt slurry, giving it a good stir before covering it and letting it sit for 10 minutes. The third ingredient you'll need is rennet. I got mine on Amazon for about four bucks. I crushed up my rennet and used a splash of bottled water. Do not use tap. I added that rennet slurry to my pot of milk, letting it sit for about 30 minutes. Rennet is an enzyme that acts on the milk proteins causing them to separate and curd like this. This is what becomes the cheese. I place my curds in a cheesecloth, squeezing out any extra liquid before adding salt to my curds and then placing my curd in a cheese mold to shape it and press it out. After 24 hours, I remove my cheese from the mold and it has this nice perfect shape. I let it air dry for a few days and I now have cheese. I'm gonna go enjoy this. Bye!
author: therealediemarie
caption: Homemade Cheddar Cheese is so easy to make 🧀! Literally from milk to magic ✨You can make it too 😍! Here’s the deets on this farmhouse cheddar cheese 🧀😍: Ingredients: 🧀 2 gallons whole milk (I used @smcdairy ) because it’s non-homogenized & not ultra-pasteurized. But any whole milk will do ! 🧀 3 tbsp plain yogurt (for culture) 🧀 3 rennet tablets (diluted in 1/2 cup of bottled water) DO NOT USE TAP WATER AS IT HAS CHLORINE IN IT! You can use VINEGAR or FRESH LEMON JUICE as a rennet substitute but the texture may be different than using rennet. 🧀 2 tsp cheese salt 1️⃣ Heat 2 gallons of milk to 90–100°F, then stir in 3 tbsp plain yogurt. Let it sit off the heat for 10 minutes. 2️⃣ Crush 3 rennet tablets and dilute with a splash of bottled water (no tap water!). 3️⃣ Add the rennet to the milk and let it sit for 30–40 minutes to form curds. 4️⃣ Scoop out the curds and gently squeeze out the whey (save it for other recipes!). 5️⃣ Mix in salt, then press the cheese in a mold or container to shape and remove extra whey. 6️⃣ Press each side for about 6 hours, or until smooth and solid. 7️⃣ Let air dry for about 2-5 days flipping the cheese on both sides to make sure it dries evenly. As the cheese dries and ages the color will change to that yellow cheese color we know and love ❤️

It backfired in the best way possible. Instead of silencing the players, it forced them to evolve. The Braun, D Wade, Mello, all traded their baggy fits for tailored suits. And then they pushed it even further. Flexing designer labels, rare sneakers and custom timepieces. A dress code that was meant to restrict self-expression ended up elevating it to a new level. The tunnel walk to a game became a runway. Players tried to one-up each other. I remember Russ breaking every fashion rule imaginable. SGA deciding to bring editorial looks to pre-game and Carl Kuzma going viral every week with a new fit. Regardless if it was good or bad. Luckily, the dress code didn't kill NBA's style. transcript: People know me for losing a leg and nearly dying in Colombia. What they don't know is what actually happened. I was riding my motorbike from the USA down to Antarctica and I was gearing up for another big day on the bike. I set off nice and early and crunched out a couple of hours riding before stopping for petrol as the sun was coming up. I sent a photo of my smiley face to the lads group chat and that's the last thing I remember before the crash. Then it gets bad. I have a flash of memory where I'm in a ditch with both my legs snapped and I think there was someone with me, maybe my guardian angel. I then recall being in a room with a wooden roof, no idea how I got there, and people trying to cut through my motorbike. Weirdly I do remember thinking to myself, have fun trying to cut through them, they're pretty strong. hook: Did you know this tip is going to blow your mind? If you cut your store-bought flowers underwater versus air, they'll last up to two weeks longer.
template: Did you know this tip, it's going to blow your mind
transcript: Did you know this tip is going to blow your mind? If you cut your store-bought flowers underwater versus air, they'll last up to two weeks longer. But why? Well, when you cut a flower stem in the open air, the exposed cut can draw air up instead of water, and the air can form a blockage within the stem's xylem. Thus, they wilt because they can't siphon water properly. You can see the tulips I cut in air versus the ones underwater. Comment below and follow me for more tips.
author: itsnicolejaques
authorName: Nicole Jaques | Low Tox Living + Cleaning + Kitchen Tips
caption: Spring flower tip: cut your stems under a base full of water or running water! Why? Cutting flowers under water, especially for blooms like lilacs and tulips, helps prevent air from entering the stems, which can block water uptake. When you cut stems in open air, tiny air bubbles can get trapped inside the vascular system, making it harder for the flowers to absorb water and stay fresh. For lilacs, which have woody stems, cutting under water helps them drink better, and you can also smash or slit the stems to improve water absorption. For tulips, which continue to grow in a vase, cutting underwater keeps them hydrated and prevents premature wilting. Basically, it’s like giving them a first-class hydration experience—spa treatment for flowers!

transcript: You would need to eat eight oranges today to get the same amount of vitamin A that your grandparents obtained from eating just one. This is because our agricultural practices focus on improving size, yield, and pest resistance rather than nutritional content. This 49-year study found declines in protein, calcium, phosphorus, iron, and vitamin C across 43 fruits and vegetables. And from 1975 to 1997, 12 other vegetables experienced a 27% decline in calcium, 37% in iron, 21% in vitamin A, and 30% in vitamin C. Another 50-year study with 20 different vegetables had similar findings. Ultimately, our food is less nutrient-rich than ever before. Now just because fruits and vegetables aren't as healthy as they used to be, it doesn't necessarily mean that we should avoid them. Hard of words, I'm talking to you. Fruits and vegetables offer a wider variety of final chemicals and antioxidants, making them our best sources for these essential compounds that help prevent disease. This is why it's so vital today that we focus on regenerative agriculture. Regenerative practices focus on restoring soil health, increasing biodiversity, and eliminating the use of chemical inputs. Healthy, living soil produces more nutrient-dense crops, reduces environmental damage, and even sequesters carbon, which helps combat climate change. By choosing food organically grown from regenerative farms, you're not only supporting practices that rebuild the nutrient cycle, but you're also ensuring better food for you and for future generations. Every bite you take is a vote for our food system. The more often we can do this, the sooner our food will be what it once was. Rich in nutrients, free of chemicals, and full of vitality.
author: denny_dure
caption: Our soil is dead, and so is the nutrient density of our food. Decades of synthetic chemicals, monocropping, and over-tilling have turned our once-living soil into lifeless dirt. Dead soil can’t retain nutrients, water, or even store carbon, and it’s why our fruits and veggies have far fewer vitamins and minerals than they did just 50 years ago. But here’s the good news: regenerative farming is the solution. Regenerative practices restore soil health by eliminating chemicals, building organic matter, and working with nature—through crop diversity, no-till farming, and grazing animals. Healthy soil doesn’t just grow healthier food; it also helps combat climate change by sequestering carbon and protecting biodiversity. Every bite you take is a vote. By choosing regeneratively grown food, you’re nourishing your body, supporting farmers who heal the earth, and investing in a healthier future for all of us. Regenerative soil = nutrient-dense food = a thriving planet. Every choice matters, shop local, choose organic, and support regenerative agriculture

hook: I spent an entire year growing garlic, but was it a waste of time? Garlic is one of the easiest foods you can grow, but it takes about 9 months before you can harvest it and once you've seen the whole life cycle, I think you're going to want to grow it too.
template: us. I spent an entire (insert time) (insert verb) but was it a waste of time?
transcript: I spent an entire year growing garlic, but was it a waste of time? Garlic is one of the easiest foods you can grow, but it takes about 9 months before you can harvest it and once you've seen the whole life cycle, I think you're going to want to grow it too. So let's get started. In late fall, we take our seed garlic and plant it with plenty of room to grow and a little fertilizer. It's important to plant as late as possible so it doesn't sprout before winter. Cover it with a blanket of mulch and wait. Once spring comes around, you'll see your garlic sprout and if you're growing hardneck garlic, it will start to produce a flower called scapes. You will pick these scapes as soon as they get curly so the plant can focus its energy on making bigger, spicier garlic underground. About 4 weeks after you pick your scapes, it's time to harvest your garlic when the bottom half of the leaves starts to turn brown. Before you brush off the dirt though, cure it in a cool dry place for a few weeks and then you can trim the stalks and clean them up. By now, it's almost time to start the whole process all over again so you can replant the biggest cloves from last year's garlic in the ground. hook: 5 ways to raise confident kids from a licensed therapist 1. Show unconditional love When kids know their worth doesn't depend on achievements, they feel free to take risks, make mistakes, and grow without fear.
template: # of ways to raise (insert adjective) children
transcript: 5 ways to raise confident kids from a licensed therapist 1. Show unconditional love When kids know their worth doesn't depend on achievements, they feel free to take risks, make mistakes, and grow without fear. Confidence thrives when kids feel secure in your love 2. Teach them to play fairly Kids who don't wait their turn, cheat, or struggle to handle losing often face rejection from peers. Play games with them to model patience, resilience, and sportsmanship. When kids play well, want to include them, boosting their confidence 3. Celebrate the process, not just the outcome. Praise how hard they studied, not just the grade they earned. Highlight how focused they were during practice, not just the win. Focusing on effort teaches kids to value what they can control, building confidence from within. 4. Let them be the teacher Switch roles and have your child teach you something. Ask curiosity-driven questions to show you value their knowledge. Teaching reinforces their belief in their abilities and helps them feel capable and respected. 5. Practice daily realistic positivity Have them share the best thing they did today, one nice thing they did for someone else, something good someone else did, a good thing happening in the world, and one thing they're looking forward to. This trains their brain to see the good in themselves, others, and the world, reinforcing a habit of looking for the good in life.
author: therapy_to_the_point
caption: 5 Ways To Raise Confident Kids

transcript: After many years of total neglect, my basement laundry room is finally getting some much needed TLC. I'm on a mission to take this spooky, filthy corner of our house and turn it into a charming little laundry nook with cottage vibes. Picture something like this, but now greatly reduce your expectations. This is not going to be a total overhaul. I'm just going to use the material that I already have on hand to make this space better than it was before. Starting with this half wall next to our washer and dryer. The rest of the basement is concrete walls, but this is the one space that we're adding drywall. Now, our 1940s home has lots of interest in characteristics, some good, some bad, but one of my favorites is this laundry shoot that comes down from the second story bathroom. I have some plans for the landing, but more to come on that later. Let's focus on the drywall. Now, like I said, the name of the game with this project is low budget. We're trying to use as much material as we have on hand without buying new. But after remodeling almost every room in our house, we have a pretty good arsenal of leftover supplies, like the wallpaper from our half bath. There wasn't enough left to do another room, but there was just the right amount for this little laundry wall. I did go to the store and buy a few things like this can of spray paint. But you know what? That's a whole lot cheaper than buying a new dryer. Once I got going with spraying things white, it was too satisfying. I couldn't stop. I even spray painted this old utility sink. Can you believe how great it turned out? I'm lying. We had to replace it. Sadly, there was no amount of spray paint that was going to save this poor old sink. The metal legs were so rusted out that the bottoms had just disintegrated. One of my least favorite things about this space is all of the exposed pipes. It gives a real basement vibe. I have an idea for how I'm going to cover them up in a way that's functional, but cute. So check back soon for another update.

He stopped selling in Italian sports stores, opting instead for exclusive boutiques in fashion capitals like Paris, Gestade, and Geneva. author: guildshore
caption: Ruffini started his career in the US, working for his father's eponymous company. When he was 23, he returned to Italy and founded a company, New England, which he sold sixteen years later to Stefanel Group. That same year, he started working as a creative consultant for the holding company which owned Moncler. In 2003, Ruffini took over Moncler, which was almost bankrupt at the time, and transformed the company by reinventing the brand. Ten years later, in December 2013, Ruffini took the company public by listing it on Milan's stock exchange. Within the first afternoon, the share price rose 47%. It was one of Italy's most successful IPOs at the time and he subsequently earned a place on the Forbes World's Billionaires list in 2014. In 2018, Ruffini conceived the Moncler Genius project, where well-known designers create collections interpreting Moncler's identity that are released on a monthly basis

hook: If you're getting older or if you have a loved one that's getting older, there are three incredibly important things that you need to make sure that you can do physically in order to live a long and healthy life. The first is making sure that you can get up off the ground by yourself with no assistance from any sort of furniture or anybody else.
template: If your getting (insert adjective) or know someone (insert adjective) there are # of incredulity important things you need to make sure you can do physically in order to (dream result)
transcript: If you're getting older or if you have a loved one that's getting older, there are three incredibly important things that you need to make sure that you can do physically in order to live a long and healthy life. The first is making sure that you can get up off the ground by yourself with no assistance from any sort of furniture or anybody else. This may sound simple, but one reason that falls can be so dangerous in elderly people other than the risk of fractures is because they can't get back up. Hence the success of the life alert "I've fallen and can't get up" commercials. Practice our kneeling push-ups and doing some supported lunges. Next is you want to be able to balance on one leg for at least 15 to 20 seconds. The better you are at balancing, the less likely you are to fall. And this is a really easy thing to practice at home. Finally, you want to make sure you have the ability to rise from a seated position without the use of pushing off your thighs or anything to pull up on. Because that is a really good sign that just the strength in your legs is enough to support your body weight without the use of anything else.
author: dr.dan_dpt
caption: In my opinion if you maintain the ability to do these three things as you age then you greatly increase your chances of maintaining a strong and healthy body for as long as you live. I started training for this challenge two years and one month ago when I could do five consecutive pull-ups and 11 pull-ups in one minute. Up until a few weeks ago the world record sat at 39 in one minute and my PB was 33 in one minute meaning I was just seven off becoming the world record holder. Then everything changed I opened Instagram and saw that the world record had been absolutely smashed to 44 making me now 12 off the title. I can't really explain the feelings that I had disheartened, shocked, proud, re-challenged, and very very distant from hitting the goal. It was a huge mental adjustment for me but I've now had time to reflect and I've made a big decision. I am now shifting my focus to train for a different world record. Half of my brain was telling me to stick at the original goal and fight for it but the other half was telling me to look at the situation in front of me and just make a logical decision. What I mean by that is when I started this challenge I really didn't have much of a clue on how to train, form and how tough breaking free plateaus would be. As I've become somewhat a little bit better in the field of pull-ups I've become a lot more aware of the requirements of each challenge. For example, in AMRAP pull-ups a wide grip minimizes the distance you need to pull making higher reps easier. High and shorter limbs also help too. Looking at the top record holders their range of motion is significantly smaller than mine. I have to pull myself up so much further each rep. Many elite athletes do pivot when they discover where their real strengths lie. Same bolt for example started as a 400 meter runner before shifting to the 100-200 meters where he became the fastest man in history. Elia Kipchoge started with the 5,000 meters before switching to the marathon where he became the first man to break two hours and my strength is when I have weights attached to me. So instead of chasing a record that isn't aligned with my strengths I'm redirecting my focus. My new girl breaking the world record for the most amount of pull-ups in one minute with a 20 pound pack and the current world record is 21. author: tombaileypt
caption: Would You Have Guessed? 🤯 Read 👇🏼 The study by Nedeltcheva et al. (2010) aimed to compare different sleep durations on weight loss, fat loss & metabolic heath 👩‍🔬 Both groups achieved similar WEIGHT loss… BUT - the 5.5 hours sleep group lost 0.6kg fat and 2.4kg lean mass 😲 Whereas the 8.5 hours sleep group lost 1.4kg fat and 1.5kg lean mass 👀 Lean mass doesn’t mean pure skeletal muscle mass tissue, it’s anything that isn’t fat but it was still shocking, so I dug deeper ⛏️ Their meal plans were a measly 18% protein and there was no mention of resistance training - 2 HUGE things for muscle retention when dieting 💪🏼 🛠️ Fixing your SLEEP makes dieting SO much easier Restricted sleep causes increases in ghrelin (hunger hormone) and decreases in leptin (satiety hormone) - so your body will be craving high calorie and sugary foods more with bad sleep! 😴 Study: Nedeltcheva AV, Kilkus JM, Imperial J, Schoeller DA, Penev PD. Insufficient sleep undermines dietary efforts to reduce adiposity. Ann Intern Med. 2010 Oct 5;153(7):435-41. doi: 10.7326/0003-4819-153-7-201010050-00006. PMID: 20921542; PMCID: PMC2951287

It looks like the last owner put hours into restoring this and then gave up. I don't even wanna know how many layers of paint were here before and I'm so grateful she started this. We're down to the last layers of black, red, and white paint and a layer of varnish. So why don't I just sandblast it or sand it? This is lead-based, so I'm left with the tedious process of stripping it by hand. This was my first go at it and you can see it's not going too well. The paint got bubbly and gummy and was not coming off clean. Definitely some smearing happening with my scraping. I had first coated the entire area with a generous amount of stripper, then went and wrapped everything in plastic and let it sit for 24 hours. But it turns out I should have put the plastic on to keep it wet as I was going instead of at the end because the stripper got too dry before I wrapped it and I believe that's why it was so gummy. I had done this to the entire entryway. I figured I should try to scrape the loose pieces before coating it again. And I guess this is how I'll spend all my nights this week. I posted my struggle on stories and one of you let me in on a pro tip that made the biggest difference. Get a ton of dollar store scrubbing pads and mineral spirits to cut the goop and get those little pieces that are in the grain of the wood. Abigail gave me hours of my life back by sending that message. So anyways, if you see me struggling through a project because of my own ignorance, save me and stay tuned to see a more satisfying banister video.

authorName: Sanju Patel | DIY from a Dad
caption: SAVE THIS: which 2x4 (or stud) shall I grab? Check the end grain. It depends on what you’re trying to do, weighed by cost and function. The truth: get creative in how to use wood by mixing and matching due to finite resources. But keep this in mind. Lumber is cut in three ways: Plain: very common because it’s easy to cut and cheaper for mills but prone to warping, twisting, cupping; it expands/contracts easily with humidity. Quarter sawn: cut perpendicular to growth rings, making it stable and stronger; great for framing key areas. If you get lucky and find one, center of trees are recommended for king studs. Rift sawn: the most stable with a uniform grain, but expensive due to waste produced
