hook: I lost both of my legs and I was only 11 months old but it's what happened after that that actually changed my life. I was born with a super rare birth defect that only happens to every few thousand babies and I was lucky enough to be one of them.
template: I (insert traumatic event) at (insert age) but it's what happened after that, that actually changed my life
transcript: I lost both of my legs and I was only 11 months old but it's what happened after that that actually changed my life. I was born with a super rare birth defect that only happens to every few thousand babies and I was lucky enough to be one of them. For the first months of my life doctors tried to straighten out my legs through force by breaking and casting my legs. You can think of it like braces for your feet. Fortunately that wasn't working at all. So soon after my parents found Shriners Hospitals for Children who suggested amputation. And traditionally they want to do it right before you're about to walk. So I was able to adapt quickly so it turned it into a pretty quick decision. At 11 months old I had both of my feet amputated but that's not what changed my life. Because in life everyone is given hardships they all look different but we all have to deal with them. And it's not about what hardship you deal with but how you react to it. Growing up I dealt with a lot of bullying. I knew I was different and kids let me know. And I think in that time I could have easily just felt sorry for myself and gave up on everything knowing that I was playing with a bad hand. But I wanted more for myself. I used to be raised in an incredible family with parents who never let me give up and brothers who pushed me to be my best and chased my dreams. And through that I found sports. I played every sport you could think of and somehow my path led me to track and field. And for the first time in my life I found a sport that nobody else could tell me how to do. A coach couldn't sit me on the bench because he was scared of me getting hurt. It was just me versus the clock. And although when I started I wasn't good at all I found so much peace in that because I finally had some control. I fell in love with pride. Just getting a little bit better each day. Working on small things over a long period of time add up to something big. And this sport has given me everything. It's taken me all over the world. It's allowed me to meet some of the most incredible people ever including my wife who infamously takes my disability lighter than anyone else that I know. But all this to say bad things will happen in your life. And there's usually two directions you can go with that. And I genuinely believe at the end of one of those roads you can look back and see that that bad thing may have been a blessing in disguise. Because if you ask me now if I would change what happened to me when I was born I'd say I wouldn't have it any other way. But if you asked me when I was trying to figure out why it happened to me I'd have a much different answer. So be yourself. It's cool to be unique. Lean into challenges. It'll make you a better person.

And we both knew that taking a big swing, meant a chance to pull off something sensational or that the wheels could come off at some point. And ultimately we miss. So it was time to be brave. And I was brave. I committed to that pace. And honestly, I had a great time until around nine miles when my body started to fight me. And that started a long solo 17 mile grind to the finish. And over those 17 miles, I went from seeing my goals slip between my fingers, the bitterness of disappointment after three months of hard work to immense gratitude. and admiration for my body. That despite the pain amplifying with every step it endured, to pride for the resilience I showed to keep going when it would have been way easier to stop. And the clearest understanding that I will be better for this. With hindsight, would I do anything differently? Absolutely not. I've gained so much from having the confidence to swing big, even if we miss this time. None of that fitness or hard work has been undone. And the growth from this race is already a part of the next chapter.
author: philybowden
caption: The London Marathon HAPPENED to me yesterday and she owes me nothing 🥲 The marathon really takes no prisoners but can also teach you more in 2.5 hours than you can learn in weeks Grateful Hungry Quite sore and tired Ready to rest and recover and ready (after that) for the next one 😈 How many of you were the ones out there cheering for me yesterday?!! Some of the messages and comments I’ve received have been incredible, I’ve hardly scratched the surface looking through them and I’m blown away. Some of you came to watch the marathon for the FIRST time, others supported from across the globe. If you were out there - thank you, and I hope you had as much “fun” as I did 🥹

There are too many lessons to fit in one video, so this is episode one of Deep in Relationships. Act through love and not through your fears. I know there's so many things you're afraid of. Will they cheat? Will they leave? Will they fall out of love? When you're afraid of losing them, you'll hold back things to protect yourself, creating distance. But there would already be distance if they were gone. So you're creating the environment as if it is already real. When you live through fear, you ask what's wrong and you're afraid of the answer. When you live through love, you ask what's wrong because you want to be there. You can't quickly change the fears you feel, but you can quickly change how you act. Act as if you are the most loved person on the planet because you already feel love and you already feel fear. You might as well act in their love. caption: a few weeks ago I realized i was making moves through fear in my own relationship. i would ask “how are you” to make sure everything is good with us, not to know how she is feeling. this seems small, but if you feel a lot of fear in you relationship it will manifest itself. this is like imagining something that makes you sick to your stomach.. you would have the same reaction if the thing actually happened. in your relationship, the thing to do is either to cling harder or distance more when you feel fear of losing them. what do you think would happen if you did lose them? you’d either beg (cling) or ghost (distance).. your fears show up in small ways when you let it consume you. but when you live through love, love can pour. How are you feels like a loving question, gifting feels like nothing attached, kind words don’t feel like prelude to something bad. let your love triumph the fear. then you make space for them to do the same. when you live in your relationship like you know they love you deeply, it feels natural to love them deeply. it’s a self sustaining cycle.. so remember: live through your love, not the fear. - @therealstain co-founder of this brand where we make cool conversation games to deeply know people

caption: Such a great snack 😏 𝘿𝙚𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙡𝙨: - 2 cups rolled oats - 1/2 cup pumpkin puree - 1/4 cup milk - 1/4 cup peanut butter (or almond butter) - 1/4 cup honey or maple syrup - 1 tsp pumpkin pie spice - 1/2 tsp baking powder - 1/2 tsp cinnamon - 1/4 tsp salt - 1/2 tsp vanilla extract - 1/3 cup chocolate chips - 1 tsp coconut oil 𝘿𝙞𝙧𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣𝙨: 1. hook: This is the amount of body fat that you would lose per day in a 250 calorie deficit. It's barely anything and it's unrecognizable.
template: This is the amount of (insert noun) you would lose per day in a (insert state)
transcript: This is the amount of body fat that you would lose per day in a 250 calorie deficit. It's barely anything and it's unrecognizable. Especially because in the same day, your body would have retained some water. So the weight of this bowl is going to be primarily water and not body fat. Then the next day, if you stay consistent, you would lose the same amount. But then again, you'd also have similar changes in water retention. This cycle will basically continue with every single day that you are in a calorie deficit. You see different changes in water retention. So after a week, you might weigh yourself and nothing is recognizable. If you stay the same, you're a little bit frustrated, but you have dropped half a pound of body fat. This is where you need to understand that losing fat and losing weight are two different things. If you're in a calorie deficit, it's going to be inevitable that you are going to drop body fat. It's impossible not to. But the water retention is always going to be all over the place. You don't really have much control over this. That's why when it comes to losing body fat, you can't just go off a weekly scale reading. Because to be honest, it doesn't really show you that much. Remember that you lose a minuscule amount of body fat per day. It comes out to about zero point six, four grams of fat that you would lose a day. You can see changes in water up to two kilograms. That's a huge difference. So you could be losing body fat, but the scale weight goes up. I know sometimes that's so hard to understand because the likes of Slim and World has led you to believe that you're only making successful fat loss if the scale weight is going down. That's why you need other measurements of progress in place like taking photos, doing measurements, going off how your clothes fit, generally going off how you feel. These will show you much more than what this would.
author: tomhullpt
caption: You CAN gain weight while losing body fat ⚖️ Think realistically… You’d lose 0.64g of body fat in a day when going into a deficit of 250 calories During the same day, you could gain 2kg of water That’s a significant difference, you’d weigh heavier whilst having less body fat So when you wake up & weigh yourself, you are going to feel like a failure and then self sabotage Because you put all of your success and self worth on a certain scale weight Of course over time the scales should drop, if you have 10kg of body fat to lose, you should be 10kg lighter by the end of that fat loss phase in 6-8 months But day to day & week to week, it wouldn’t change loads So make sure you take this into consideration if you are currently on your weight loss journey Take other measurements of progress & not just scale weight

hook: This small fish gets eaten by a bigger fish, which gets eaten by an even bigger fish, which gets eaten by an even bigger fish, and that's how the food chain moves. But let's rewind.
template: This (insert adjective) (insert noun) gets (insert verb) by this (insert adjective) (insert noun)
transcript: This small fish gets eaten by a bigger fish, which gets eaten by an even bigger fish, which gets eaten by an even bigger fish, and that's how the food chain moves. But let's rewind. Small fish like sardines or anchovies, which are typically filter feeders, meaning they eat plankton and algae, but also tiny amounts of microplastics, biotoxins, and mercury that's floating around in the water. Then a mid-sized fish like a mackerel or snapper doesn't just eat one sardine. It eats around 500 of these small fish per year, and with every bite it absorbs the nutrients from the small fish, but also the toxins that the small fish collected. Now a tuna, a much bigger fish, eats 100 of these mid-sized fish per year. This is why a big tuna compared to a sardine can have over 50 times more mercury. This process is called bioaccumulation, and that's when toxins build up over time. But when a predator eats hundreds of contaminated fish, those toxins multiply, and this process is called biomagnification. And that's why the biggest fish like sharks, swordfish, and king mackerel have the highest mercury levels in the ocean. The bigger the fish, the bigger the risk. So when it comes to fish, I like to follow smash, the five fish that are low in mercury and high in omega-3s. That's sardines, mackerel, anchovies, salmon, and herring. These fish sit lower on the food chain, meaning they don't accumulate nearly as many toxins, making them some of the best choices for both nutrition and sustainability.
author: michaeltchao
caption: BIG FISH… BIG RISK? 🐟 Not all fish are equal. The food chain dictates mercury levels, and the bigger the fish, the more mercury it accumulates. If you’re looking for the healthiest seafood choices, follow SMASH: Sardines Mackerel Anchovies Salmon Herring

Just make sure that you don't place the nodes too far away from each other or you'll still have some issues. But if your budget is really tight and your place is small, then Wi-Fi extenders are fine, but for bigger homes, a mesh network is so much better.
author: gg.sheed
caption: Do you use a WiFi Extender or Repeater? 🤔 WiFi repeaters do boost your signal but often have slower speeds since it uses the same channels as your main router. WiFi Extenders fix this issue with slowness, but create their own separate network which can be annoying to deal with if you have devices moving around. The best way to extend your wireless network would be to use Access Points or a mesh WiFi network. Mesh networks are a collection of nodes placed around your house that all talk to each other and boost the signal for the network across your entire home. Also you don’t have to manage which one you’re connected to

hook: After 6 months of research, here's why I choose Icorn flower and started milling my own. Icorn is one of the oldest greens and unlike modern weed, it's completely unhybridized.
template: After (insert time frame) of research here is why I choose (insert noun) and started (insert action)
transcript: After 6 months of research, here's why I choose Icorn flower and started milling my own. Icorn is one of the oldest greens and unlike modern weed, it's completely unhybridized. This means it retains its original genetic structure, making it much easier for our bodies to digest. Icorn has just 14 chromosomes while modern weed has around 42, which is part of the reason why many people find modern weed harder on their digestive system. It has essential minerals like zinc, iron, and magnesium. Plus, it has a rich nutty flavor that makes everything taste better. By milling and corn at home, I can preserve all its natural oils and nutrients, which are often lost in processed or bought flowers. While investing in a grain mill, which starts around $400 in Icorn greens, about $3 per pan requires some upfront cost, but I believe it's well worth it.
author: littlehealthyplates
caption: My journey with einkorn flour began while searching for solutions for my daughter’s acute eczema. I was initially exploring flour-free options, but during my research, I came across einkorn flour—a type of ancient wheat I had never heard of before. Curious, I did a deep dive into its benefits, and what I discovered was fascinating. Einkorn wheat is one of the oldest grains and hasn’t been hybridized like modern wheat. It grows naturally in harsh environments without the need for chemical fertilizers, which I learned can often trigger or worsen conditions like eczema. Its simple genetic structure (just 14 chromosomes compared to modern wheat’s 42) makes it gentler on digestion and packed with nutrients like protein, zinc, iron, and magnesium. Plus, it has a rich, nutty flavor that’s hard to beat. At first, I bought pre-milled einkorn flour, as grain mills can be a big investment. But after some time, I decided to purchase my own mill—and it’s been one of the best decisions I’ve made. Milling the grains myself means I get the freshest flour, full of its natural oils and nutrients, and I can really taste the difference in everything I bake. If you’re considering trying einkorn flour, I recommend doing your own research to see if it’s the right fit for you. It’s been a game-changer for my family, and I couldn’t be happier with the switch!

transcript: Do you feel suffocated by your home's constant creep of clutter? Clutter gets a bad rap, but for most people, it's just your daily essentials resurfacing because they're not stored in the most functional way. On day seven of living smarter, not harder, let's dig into clutter and share your clutter creep in the comments below. Our belongings fall into two categories. Things you show, items organized into visible spots like tables, counters, and hooks, and the things you stow, items tucked into drawers, cabinets, and closets. Finding the right balance of shows and stows enables you to effortlessly put things away, quickly clean up messes, stick to important habits, and most importantly, feel at ease in your own home. So move through each space and be intentional about what stays out and why. Finding your ideal balance between aesthetics, convenience, and visual cues, like should your meds live on the counter or in a drawer. Keep them out for a visual reminder or tuck them away if a daily alarm works just fine. Should sunglasses stay out and add to visual clutter or be stowed and risked forgotten on a sunny day. You probably don't need the visual cue for tea, but if your kettle is far from your drawers, keeping it out could add valuable convenience. And maybe with that persistent mail pile, seeing it daily only triggers dread instead of action. So consider tucking it away with a weekly reminder to sort through it. This system evolves over time. If something you stowed keeps reappearing, it's probably a sign it should be organized into the shows. And this process makes you more intentional about which items add value to your daily life so you can regularly go through and downsize those untouched stows. And now that we have this mental model in the next video, let's dive into practical ways to organize your shows and your stows.

hook: The lack of clinical studies on tallow isn't because it doesn't work. It's because big brands don't see a profit in it.
template: The lack of clinical studies on (insert noun) isn't because it doesn't work, it's because…
transcript: The lack of clinical studies on tallow isn't because it doesn't work. It's because big brands don't see a profit in it. Most skincare studies are funded by companies looking to patent their products. But for a product to be patented, it has to be novel, non-obvious, and man-made. Tallow is none of these things. It's simply beef fat, a naturally occurring substance that hasn't been chemically altered and has been used for centuries. Because of this, it can't be patented. And if a company can't patent an ingredient, they can't own it or monopolize it. So instead of studying tallow, the beauty industry focuses on synthetic alternatives they can trademark, mass-produce, and sell as exclusive innovations. And that's a shame because tallow is one of the most skin-compatible ingredients out there. Its fatty acids are already well-documented for their skincare benefits in their isolated forms. And in their natural state, like in tallow, they are even more bioavailable, making it one of the most effective moisturizers you can use.
author: lilyhilltallowco
caption: While there may not be may clinical trials on tallow itself, the fatty acids it contains, like oleic acid and stearic acid, are well-documented for their skincare benefits. And in their natural, unaltered state, like in tallow, they are potentially even more bioavailable

hook: You're not bad at fashion. You probably just haven't been taught how to put an outfit together.
template: You are not bad at (insert action), you probably were just never taught how to (insert action)
transcript: You're not bad at fashion. You probably just haven't been taught how to put an outfit together. This is episode five of Find Your Personal Style in 10 Days. You see, great style isn't about owning the cutest pieces. It's about how those pieces interact with each other. You can have the coolest, most expensive clothes on the planet. But if you don't know how to put them together, who cares? First, let's talk about shape balance. Every great outfit is a mix of structure versus softness, fitted versus oversized. If your outfit is all structured, it can look stiff. If it's all relaxed, it can look shapeless. Mixing up the shapes in silhouette is a great way to create a balanced and more intentional look. Next, let's talk about texture contrast. Outfits feel flat when every piece has the same texture. A little contrast adds dimension. A knit sweater with leather shorts? Fabulous. A light blouse with structured denim? Sickening! Next, let's talk about proportion. This is what makes an outfit feel effortless instead of awkward. Proportions are about how different parts of your outfit interact. If everything is the same length or volume, the look can feel flat and uninteresting. And if the pieces don't complement each other, it might feel awkward or look like it was just thrown together haphazardly. Think of it like interior design. When elements are arranged with the right balance, a space feels intentional. And outfits work the same exact way. When proportions flow, your outfit feels cohesive. When they clash, something just feels off. The key is to create balance between the pieces so that the eye moves naturally. Save this video for later if it helped, and tune in tomorrow for Why Accessories Matter. Don't miss it.
author: aasian
caption: ever wonder why some outfits feel effortlessly put together while others just… don’t? 👀 it’s not just about the clothes—it’s about how you put them together. balance, structure, and proportion all play a role in making an outfit work. here’s how to break it down: 📌 structure vs. flow – balance fitted + relaxed pieces for an effortless look. 📌 texture & contrast – mixing fabrics (like leather, denim, or knits) + light vs. dark, soft vs. bold—contrast makes outfits interesting. 📌 proportions – where pieces hit on your body changes how an outfit feels. the best outfits feel good because they’re intentionally balanced. so next time something looks “off,” try tweaking structure, layering, or contrast instead of changing your whole wardrobe! if you have any questions about the outfits in these videos, feel free to ask in the comments and i’ll try to find the exact pieces or link you to something similar if i can find a dupe :)

hook: Does it actually matter which type of flour you choose? To show you the difference that flour choice can make, I made one loaf of bread with four different doughs.
template: Does it actually matter what type of (insert noun) you use
transcript: Does it actually matter which type of flour you choose? To show you the difference that flour choice can make, I made one loaf of bread with four different doughs. Flour is mostly made up of protein and starch in different ratios. And even tiny changes in that ratio will have huge effects on the final product. That's why you'll often see protein percentage labeled in big, bold numbers on the front of the bag. Hard flours like bread and whole wheat have more protein and produce more gluten for a stronger internal structure and a chewier dough. Good for things like bread, bagels, pitas, pasta, or pizza. Soft flours like pastry or cake flour have less protein and more starch, which absorbs water and helps things like muffins, cheesecake, or banana bread stay moist and crumbly after baking. An all-purpose flour is right down the middle, which makes it a safe choice for all purposes.

hook: A quick guide to cutting vegetables. Some basic and some unusual.
template: A quick guide to (insert verb) (insert noun) some basic and some unusual
transcript: A quick guide to cutting vegetables. Some basic and some unusual. Beginning with the classic dice of an onion which starts with cutting the stem but leaving the root. Then making vertical cuts from stem to root and then chopping into chunks. Great for stews or braces. For a finer dice make horizontal cuts and increase the number of vertical cuts. Leaving you with much smaller chunks of onion that are great for vinaigrettes or sauces. Followed by that as a half ring simply cutting half an onion horizontally. Or try the crescent cut that involves cutting from root to stem instead of side to side. Followed by that is the julienne. Cutting vegetables into strips then slicing lengthways for thin strands. Go one step further and cut those strips into small cubes called brunoise. Cutting spring onions at a 45 degree angle gets you beautiful oval slivers. Similarly if you cut them into two sections harden them twice and put them into cold water you get these beautiful curly strands that are also great for garnishing. For herbs particularly with large leaves like basil you can roll them into a bunch and finely cut from top to bottom to get the chiffonade. Or roll into a bunch chop through once like a chiffonade but then rock your knife over the pile one to two times for a dice. Both great for garnishing or stirring into sauces. For all these cutting techniques good form is essential to get the best result and also keep you safe. Try searching up the popular claw method which I'm showing here. you

transcript: My boyfriend and I moved in together and ended up losing $20,000 in less than 10 minutes. I could barely hear him, the reception was terrible, so all I caught him say was run home now. I had no idea what was happening, but his voice sounded different, so I just ran. And the second I turned the corner to my building, my stomach dropped. Fire trucks, firefighters, half the building evacuated. I pushed inside and all I heard was pipe bursts, flooding, and then a fire firefighters said my apartment number. And that's when it hit me that we never got renters insurance. By the time I made it upstairs, it was already over. Black water everywhere, a massive hole in our ceiling from where the pipe exploded. The journal I'd been writing in every day for the past four years, gifts from my grandparents, a hard drive filled with 20 years of family photos. What made it worse was that this wasn't even our fault. A building pipe burst out of nowhere, and now we're the ones paying for it. And to make things worse, we were so close to being covered. My boyfriend almost finished getting renters insurance the day before he left for our trip. But I was already on a flight to Nepal, so he decided to wait to ask me how much to insure for jewelry. template: If you see (insert symptom), (insert symptom) especially on a (insert type of noun) you better worry about what's called (insert name)
transcript: If you have red inflamed eyes, maybe a little bit of a loudness to the cornea, and especially if you see it on a brachycephalic or shark face breed, one of the things you have to worry about is what's called KCS, or dry eye. That is a condition where the dog doesn't make enough tears, so the eye literally becomes dry and inflamed and irritated. So if you have KCS and it goes untreated, you'll get blood vessels and you'll get pigment from the outside of the eye, from the sclera, and it'll bridge that cornea and it just causes a blockage to where they physically can't see, and that would be just like us looking through a dirty window.
author: waggintrainvet
caption: 👇 more crucial info 🐶 What is it? Keratoconjunctivitis, or “dry eye,” is a condition where your dog’s eyes don’t produce enough tears to stay moist and healthy. It’s especially common in brachycephalic breeds (those adorable smoosh-faced dogs like Pugs, Bulldogs, and Shih Tzus). 👁️ Signs to Watch For: Red or irritated eyes Thick, sticky discharge Excessive blinking or squinting Cloudy or dull-looking eyes Pawing at their face 💦 Why It Happens: Those sweet flat faces often come with shallow eye sockets or other features that lead to tear gland issues. Without enough tears, the eyes can dry out and become irritated, leading to discomfort and even vision problems. 🛠️ What Can Be Done? Your vet may prescribe lubricating drops or ointments. In some cases, medication is needed to stimulate tear production. 🩺 Don’t Wait! Take your dog to the vet if you notice any of these signs. Catching it early means faster relief for your pup! Healthy eyes = a happy dog. 🐾

transcript: I haven't washed my face in over two years and it's healed my skin. For reference, this is what it used to look like. It's super oily with a bunch of clogged pores. So I'm going to show you what my natural nighttime skincare routine looks like using natural and minimal products. Our skin produces its own natural oils called sebum, which is there to maintain a healthy skin moisture barrier. And it's also antibacterial. But when we're washing our face morning and night and just using overall harsh, generic skincare, we're completely stripping your skin of its moisture. So to counteract that, it's going to produce even more sebum. That's what's going to give us that oily look. So sebum isn't the issue. The overproduction of sebum is. So instead, what I do is that a couple of nights a week, I'll do a raw honey face mask. This is great to draw moisture into the skin and also has great antibacterial properties. I then rinse my face with water in the shower and moisturize with beef towel. It's bioidentical to the sebum or skin produces. So it makes it deeply moisturizing and nourishing. I really like it because it's very gentle on my skin without irritating it. Lastly, on the days that I wear makeup, I like to oil cleanse. It melts everything off. And that is my super minimal and natural skincare routine.
author: thrivewithcandicee
caption: My natural & minimal skincare routine 👇🏻 Quick reminder that your “skincare” primarily comes from the INSIDE ! If I’m wearing makeup, I remove it with an oil before - moisturize with beef tallow (my favorite brand is from small business @elaskincare.co code CANDICE10 gets you a discount) You only need a very thin layer so start off small ! - a few times a week I also dry brush my face to naturally exfoliate and promote lymphatic drainage, but the wash cloth by itself already does a great job ! And that’s it - super minimal yet nourishing ! But most importantly I let my skin do it’s OWN THING :)

Good thing my egg white oats check every box. Yes, they smell a bit questionable, but no, they don't taste like egg. (upbeat music) Start with 30 grams of oats cooked in your liquid of choice. I use water and a pinch of salt, and I use milk. Then, measure out 200 grams of egg whites. Yes, you can use boxed egg whites. No, in Scotland, they are not cheaper. I did the math. So instead, my cat and dog get the yolks. Egg whites are a complete, highly digestible protein source with an ideal amino acid profile, which basically means eating them will make us big and strong. Once measured, add the egg whites to your oats and whisk. And when I say whisk, I mean put your whole elboussey into it. If you stop, you'll end up with scrambled egg oats. They'll froth up at first, and then thicken. Once it looks less terrifying, add in one host of eggs, whole egg, and whisk again. The yolk makes it creamier and adds extra micronutrients. Time for the add-ins. I go for vanilla extract, almond extract, walnuts, and banana. But honestly here, you can add whatever you want, apart from protein powder, because no one deserves that kind of suffering. Once the banana has caramelized, I top with almond butter and sweet cinnamon. 35 grams of protein, ridiculously filling, and not a single grain of protein powder in sight. The most delicious and stinky way to start your day.

caption: my FAVOURITE high protein breakfast 🥹💕✨ Egg White Oats Recipe: 34G Protein 30G Oats 200G Egg White 1 Whole Egg Vanilla Extract. + Almond Extract 5G Walnuts 40G Banana 10G Almond Butter

hook: The worst thing you can do for your hair is to ignore your hair porosity when choosing products. The good news is that it's super easy to find your hair porosity and all you need is a piece of hair and a glass of water.
template: Worst thing you can do for your (insert thing) is to ignore your (insert noun) when (insert scenario)
transcript: The worst thing you can do for your hair is to ignore your hair porosity when choosing products. The good news is that it's super easy to find your hair porosity and all you need is a piece of hair and a glass of water. Hair porosity is your hair's ability to absorb and retain moisture. The openness of your hair cuticles will determine how well your hair will retain water and nutrients. So take a cup of water and place a single strand of hair into it. If your hair floats, then you probably have low porosity hair. Porosity hair has tightly packed cuticles, so you need to make sure you're picking products that won't weigh your hair down. If your hair sinks, then you probably have high porosity hair. High porosity hair has very open cuticles that lose moisture easily. So you need to pick products that add hydration back into the hair shaft. And if it's in between, then you probably have normal or medium porosity hair. Comment on this video your hair porosity and I'll give you recommendations for your hair.
author: kiyoko.beauty
caption: Struggling with your hair? 🌊 Find out your porosity with just a strand of hair and a glass of water! 🧪 💧 Floats? Low porosity—go for lightweight products. 🌊 Sinks? High porosity—focus on hydration. Comment your porosity [HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM] for product recs!

If you want your press-on nails to look and last like salon nails, prepping your nails, how the salon usually preps your nails. The next mistake that I see people make is using cheap nails. Trust me, I've been there too. If you can bend your nails and they are flimsy or they bend or they crack, those are not good nails. They won't hold up. One of my favorite brands to use that has affordable high quality nails is Nail Reformation, Olive and June, Impress, Be Artbok, and Glamnetic. Those are all amazing ones. Third and final mistake that I see people make has to do with the glue that you're using. And I tell you, I've tried every single nail glue brand. It's the only one I religiously use and recommend. It is literally six to nine dollars. It is called the beauty secrets drip proof nail glue, literally cement for your nails. My nails will not come off for 30 days. And I've proven that to you time and time again. 12 out of 10 recommend. Just a bonus tip for you guys. Application is truly the most important thing. Honestly, I just add glue to my natural nail. I take the press-on nail at a 45 degree angle, push it back into my cuticle, push down, hold it for 30 seconds. Too many of you guys just hold it for five seconds and release it. hook: Ever wonder how the same ingredients can result in drastically different cookies? Keep your guide into what causes different variations in cookies and what to look for in a recipe.
template: Every wonder how the same (insert noun) can result in drastically different (insert noun)
transcript: Ever wonder how the same ingredients can result in drastically different cookies? Keep your guide into what causes different variations in cookies and what to look for in a recipe. For a more standard chewy soft cookie that spreads, look for a cookie recipe that has a high ratio of fat and sugar to flour. The sugar and fat will cause the cookies to spread more as there isn't a strong structure to hold the shape. For a thin delicate airy crunchy cookie, choose a recipe that has a low protein flour and reverse creaming. Reverse creaming is when you mix flour and fat together before adding liquid or sugar. The fat coats the flour creating this barrier from liquid giving the delicate texture. For a thick cookie, choose a recipe that has a higher ratio of flour to sugar and fat. Cream the butter and sugar together and you want to make sure that the recipe has a high protein flour like bread or whole wheat. Whole wheat absorbs more liquid than all-purpose so it's going to create a chewy cookie that will spread less.

transcript: If you're blending coloured pencils like this, you're doing it wrong. This is the most common mistake I see beginner artists make when trying to draw smooth coloured pencil gradients like this. The key to a smooth blend isn't your pencil brand and it isn't even how many layers you use. It's about how you overlap your colours. Instead of each colour sitting side by side, then trying to force them together, overlap them more, gradually lightening your pressure as each colour crosses over the next. And hold your pencil further back if you're finding it hard to lighten your pressure. With a little practice, you'll be able to blend coloured pencils like a pro.

I want you to go on Google, look up "TDEE calculator" and that is how you are going to find your calorie deficit. You're going to input all of your information, your height, your weight, your activity level. Now it's going to give you a maintenance. You're going to want to subtract about 100-200 from that number to get your calorie deficit number. Okay, where do I even begin? You want to prioritize protein in every single meal. Take up 30 grams of protein. Lunch 30 grams of protein. 3/4 of a cup of Greek yogurt is 18 grams of protein. Add a scoop of protein powder. It's 30 grams right there. 3 ounces of deli turkey. In a wrap. Easy. On the go. It comes that much easier to stay full, stay satiated. It will help you lose fat and keep muscle. Number three, strength training. It might be a little scary. It might be a little daunting. I promise once you pick up a weight, you will see how fast that weight starts flying off. You will be burning calories in after your workout because it's with strength training. It does. That's what lifting weights does. You just strength train and do nothing else and don't prioritize your calorie deficit or protein or your steps or your cardio. Not going to help. All of these things mixed together is the key for fat loss. I've done it. Start off with three to four times a week. It doesn't have to be crazy. Find a workout split that works for you, you love, and that you enjoy, that you could see yourself doing long-term. Isn't just a quick fix. It's a lifestyle change. The fourth thing, your steps. I didn't realize how much walking has changed my physique and my body and my mental health and my clarity. I used to get like three, four thousand steps a day. Now that I am aware of my steps for a 10 minute walk after lunch, a thousand steps. Buy a walking pad, wake up 10 minutes earlier, another thousand steps. It helps you digest. You're not as inflamed. My body just loves it. It craves it. It craves movement. Like make that your you time. I go on walks to think about my life, think about what my goal is, what my why is, why am I walking? Why am I doing all these things? Because I want to become the best version of myself. And I know that if I invest in myself and pour into myself, it will pour back into me eventually. If you are tracking everything you're eating, you're in your calorie deficit, you're moving your body, you're getting your steps in. The first two weeks are the hardest. You're going to be like, this isn't working. This isn't for me. After that like two, three week mark, the weight will melt off. It is an addictive feeling. But once you start, will not want to stop. It's been four years now. And I have maintained this body can get there and you can do it too. Lessons I've learned from losing 30. hook: If you want to lose fat, running is the worst thing that you can do. I've been running now for a month and since starting, my appetite has gone through the roof and I've actually gained weight.
template: If you want to (insert dream result), (insert action) is the worst thing you can do
transcript: If you want to lose fat, running is the worst thing that you can do. I've been running now for a month and since starting, my appetite has gone through the roof and I've actually gained weight. I've been an online coach for six years and in that time have completed numerous fat loss phases for both myself and my clients. One thing I've never programmed and never will do for fat loss is running. Why? Because when you're running, your body burns a lot more calories and your body's carbohydrate store gets emptied. This ramps up your body's appetite as it wants to replenish the carbohydrates it's burned, making sticking to the amount of calories you need to lose fat very hard. So what cardio should you do instead? Walk. It's the most powerful fat loss tool and the best cardio you can do for fat loss. Why? Because it doesn't require anywhere near as much glycogen as running, so your appetite won't massively spike. It's also low impact on the body, meaning your body can easily recover from it alongside any weight training you're doing, unlike running which is high impact on the body. I'm not shitting on running, I actually enjoy it. I'm just making you aware that if your main goal is fat loss, running will make it harder.
author: bencarter1
caption: Being in my running era right now, I think it’s important to give this reminder… Walking > running for fat loss

hook: I got engaged at 20 and got married by 21. If you're scared about marriage, this is for you.

transcript: I got engaged at 20 and got married by 21. If you're scared about marriage, this is for you. My name is Estee and you might be following me because of my music or my covers. But today I wanted to share my experience on what it's like to be married young. So here's three things I've learned as a young wife in our early 20s. The first thing is that it really feels like you're growing up together. As happy as I was to be getting married to my best friend, I actually cried a lot during our engagement because this was the first time either of us has ever moved out of home. There was a lot of change that comes with moving away from your family and starting a new one together. I very quickly had to learn how to be independent while also leaning into our new dynamic of being married. The second thing I learned is that the way that you treat your spouse plays a huge role in who they eventually are. I was a completely different person when we first got married compared to who I am. Looking back, I actually feel like I don't even recognize myself. He always chose to love me even during the hardest moments of our lives. The third thing is that our individual relationships with God ultimately makes our marriage what it is today. Especially coming from an Asian background, people in my life are actually more concerned than excited for us to get married. Just because we were so young. There was a lot of gossip going around. But the reason why I had so much hope for our future together, despite not even knowing what exactly might happen, is because we knew God and we knew we could trust Him, which made it easier to just be excited for the good plans He has for us. I love my husband and I'm grateful to God every day for bringing us together. It's almost been two years and God has already done so much. So I'm just excited to see what else He does.
author: estee.evangeline
caption: i used to be really scared of the idea that one day you could just wake up and fall out of love but it’s kinda crazy how untrue that is lol if you’re an overthinker like me and worry a lot, i just wanted to be an example that there’s hope for your future ! here’s 3 reasons why getting married was one of the best things i’ve ever done 💒 (also i am no expert i am still a baby LOL but this has been my experience 🙈) 1. i’m growing up with my bestest friend 2. i have someone constantly speaking life into me and helping me grow into the person God created me to be 3. going about our relationship God’s way has brought God’s blessing, favour, and protection over our lives; we always knew we could rely on Him for our future i’m a firm believer that choosing each other everyday and having God at the centre of your relationship is what makes a marriage so strong, and i think that’s how God designed it to be! it’s also helped me be more confident, understanding God’s love for me more and more as time goes on 🩷 some people think getting married is the end of everything but it’s actually just the beginning, and it’s the best feeling getting to spend the rest of your life with your best friend <3

hook: Here's how the form of butter that you add into cookies affects them. I made four batches of chocolate chip cookies where the only thing I changed in the recipe was the form of the butter.
template: Here's how the form of (insert noun) you add into (insert noun) affects them
transcript: Here's how the form of butter that you add into cookies affects them. I made four batches of chocolate chip cookies where the only thing I changed in the recipe was the form of the butter. I test a softened butter, melted butter, browned melted butter, and browned softened butter. I just cooled it down and stirred it until it's a softened butter consistency. The softened butter cookie dough turned out pale and creamy. It's a classic cookie dough. Melted butter made a cookie dough that was much darker. Butter is anywhere from 80 to 85% fat. So when you brown it, you get rid of about 10 to 15% of moisture. This resulted in a drier, almost crumbly cookie dough when I used melted brown butter and softened brown butter. We all got baked at the same temperature for the same amount of time. Softened butter had the thinnest cookie with the most amount of spread, with the softest melty center, and a classic chocolate chip cookie flavor. Melted butter had the second most amount of spread, a much thicker cookie, and had the most amount of browning. It had much crispier edges and also had a caramelized cookie flavor. The middle was still soft, but not quite as soft as the softened butter. Melted brown butter had the least amount of spread, the thickest cookie, and crisp all the way around the outside, not just the edges. The very center was still gooey and had a caramelized cookie and brown butter flavor. Softened brown butter cookies spread more than the previous, with the least amount of browning and a very crisp buttery exterior. It tasted like brown butter shortbread with a soft center. Which type of cookie do you prefer? And check out the caption for details on the science behind these results.
author: flouringkitchen
caption: This is how softened butter, melted butter, and browned butter affect cookies! Can you believe that this is the same recipe and that the only thing I changed was the form of butter that I used? Both the softened butter and the softened browned butter resulted in cookies with more spreading and less browning than their melted butter counterparts. This can be because of the process of creaming butter and sugar together. Incorporating a lot of air into the cookies creates a cookie that is more insulated because air is an insulator. This prevents flour from cooking quickly in the oven, allowing the cookie to spread more and prevents browning. For a longer video breakdown with more details on the differences and cookie science behind these results, check out my bio link ❤️ I know you’re going to ask soooooo: I preferred the melted browned butter cookie the most because of the caramelized cookie and browned butter flavor. So good! Produced with the participation of the @cmf.fmc

When it comes to losing weight, it’s not just about making more nutritious choices than you otherwise might—it’s also about making sure you’re eating fewer calories than you burn each day. No matter how nutritious your diet is, if you’re not in a calorie deficit, you won’t lose weight. Share this with any friends that love açai bowls

author: jeeves_ny
caption: This is a dry cleaners guide for depilling your garments! It’s important to remember that the action of depilling is removing material from your garment. The harder you comb, the more that will come off. This can cause premature damage and holes if you’re too rough. 1) The Restora depilling comb is a classic that’s inexpensive, small, and easy to use 2) I love the Gleener depilling comb and lint brush combo because it gives you a ton of versatility and you can sweep up the pills after with the lint brush 3) The sweater shaver is always a good time but you should be careful on delicate / thing items 4) A disposable razor will help in a pinch but won’t be very efficient or effective 5) Uproot makes one too but I find it too aggressive for clothing I hope this helps! Thank you @wangjenniferr for the intro inspo

But for me this move isn't about finding myself, it's about being able to be myself. I want to live in a culture where I don't have to justify waking up at 5am, working out, watching the sunrise, going to bed at 8.30, fueling my body with foods which make me feel good. And I already know these make me happy, I just want an environment which encourages this lifestyle. Obviously I'll miss things from the UK, my family and percy pigs but if I stay in an environment which doesn't support my happiness I'm only hurting myself. So yes this move is terrifying and I have no idea what's ahead. And honestly it feels selfish but it's my life. I realise there's no point spending it in the what if zone when I could be living in that I'm doing this. And who knows maybe I hate it and I'll come crawling back but if I never try I'll never know. So here is your sign, if your environment is holding you back whether it's moving cities, cutting out toxic people, switching jobs, you have the power to change it. hook: If I had to start over and train my back from scratch, these are the exercises I would do for someone that's new to training and maybe get featured in Dori's commercial. The most important thing to know is, what do your lats actually do?
template: If I had to start over and (insert verb) my (insert noun) from scratch, these are the only (insert noun) I would do for someone that is new to (insert noun)
transcript: If I had to start over and train my back from scratch, these are the exercises I would do for someone that's new to training and maybe get featured in Dori's commercial. The most important thing to know is, what do your lats actually do? And there's a few things. Shoulder reduction, where you bring your arms down to your side, and shoulder extension, where you bring your arms back and away from the front side of your body. These are the two exercises that I always include to help me grow my back. Single arm pull down. You can do this on a lat pull down machine, but I prefer using an incline bench next to a cable machine. It allows me to easily adjust my position by moving the pulley or bench and it just feels better overall. The benefit of using one arm is that you can achieve great range of motion and build a stronger mind muscle connection compared to using both arms. Not that there's anything wrong with using both arms, but do you know anyone who uses both hands to jerk off? Chest supported rows. Why chest supported? The added stability cues you from worrying about your lower back taking over, which can happen with exercises like barbell or dumbbell rows. This setup really helps isolate your lats and encourages strict form. But if your gym doesn't have one, try alternatives like helms row or setting up an incline bench for a smith machine rows. They're great substitutes that still get the job done.

hook: How long can you skip the gym before losing muscle? Building muscle takes time.
template: How long can you skip (insert action) before losing (insert result)
transcript: How long can you skip the gym before losing muscle? Building muscle takes time. Once it's there, your body doesn't want to lose it unless it has a reason to. So let's say you do take two to three weeks off the gym due to vacation, getting sick, or just life getting in the way. You might notice your muscles looking smaller or feeling a little bit puffier, but there's good news. During that time when you're feeling smaller, it's not actually muscle that you're losing. It's water and glycogen stored in the muscles that's making them look full. And the best part, as soon as you get back into the gym, a couple of workouts will fill them right back up. Now, what if you take longer than three weeks? If you're out for more than three weeks, you'll probably start to lose muscle. But here's where things get good. Muscle memory is real. Your body remembers the muscle that it had. So getting back to where you were happens way faster than the first time you built it. Think of it like unlocking a shortcut. Two to six weeks, and boom, you're back to normal. So if you've missed a few workouts recently, don't let your mind trick you into thinking you lost all your progress. That's just the body dysmorphia talking. Now, if this makes sense and you want to get your nutrition dialed in, Comment gains down below and I'll send you my free calorie macro calculator.

transcript: I crammed for the hardest CS midterm and scored in top 10%. I'm definitely not one of those CS kids that knew how to code before they can walk. So while I knew I only had 48 hours to study, I implemented a strategy that actually worked. The first step was to consume all the material incrementally through watching the lectures. There was approximately 6 lectures and took 12 hours in total. I also created my own notes to structure my thinking across the entire unit and compared it with the lecture notes. That brings the second tip of understanding the same topic through different mediums, for example, linked lists. You read the properties in the application through lecture notes. I spent a good 46 hours going through the labs, which is the actual programming part. I then tested my understanding through the four practice exams, which took approximately eight hours. It's really important to go in without looking at the answer and mimic the exam environment. Another really good tip from my TA was to diagram, having the pointers, the memory storage, how it was being traversed, visualized. On the day of the exam, I quickly went through all the material, including the labs, my notes, and the practice exam. When the clock hit zero, I kinda knew I ate.

hook: Here are my money rules as a non-frugal 29 year old working towards financial independence. Number one, buy cheap before investing in high quality items.
template: My money rules as a (insert description) working towards financial independence
transcript: Here are my money rules as a non-frugal 29 year old working towards financial independence. Number one, buy cheap before investing in high quality items. You know, they're saying your eyes are bigger than your stomach. Well, that's me with pretty much everything. I love getting the best of the best, but nine times out of 10, I buy an expensive item and then I never use it or never wear it. So now I'll buy cheap to make sure it's something that I actually value. And if it is, then I'll invest in a higher quality item. And I know it sounds counterintuitive, but this has saved me thousands of dollars and the hassle of trying to resell things. Number two, overspending is okay as long as you correct yourself afterwards. Many money for me ebbs and flows. Some months I spend way more than average and some I spend very little. I think of spending on an average across the entire year. Instead of zooming into a specific week or month, the more strict I am about my finances, the more likely I am to overspend. And number three, never adjust how much goes into savings or investments to pay off overspending. For me, reducing my savings or investments to cover overspending is a very slippery slope. There are many months I have so many negative categories in my budget, but I know if the buffer in my checking account is positive, I don't have to worry about paying my bills or overdrafting. I'll just dial back my spending in those categories to make up for it over the next couple of months.
author: mckenzie.mack_
caption: my money rules as a non-frugal 29 year old working towards financial independence 💸📈 1️⃣ buy cheap first, quality later *this only applies to things I’m not 100% sure about, if I know I will use and love an item I skip the cheap stuff Doc Martens are a real life example for me - I wanted these boots for MONTHS before I bought them and when I finally did I literally never wore them. The issue was I don’t wear boots !!!! I wish I would have bought a cheap pair that looked almost exactly the same so I could see how often I reached for them and wore them before buying an expensive pair. I ended up reselling the boots and made maybe 75% of my money back 😅 This is also a good way to see if you want something just because its name brand, you want people to know you have it, or if you actually love it for yourself. 2️⃣ overspending is fine as long as you correct afterwards I can be a big overspender sometimes, but if I feel guilty about my spending I tend to overspend even more. Instead of beating myself up about it, I set up systems that allow me to make mistakes without the risk - keeping one month’s worth of expenses in my checking account is an example of this. 3️⃣ never sacrifice savings or investments to pay off overspending this doesn’t apply for actual emergencies, just for normal overspending and going over budget in my categories. I have done this in the past and it is definitely a slippery slope. If I reduce my savings or investments once, I tend to do it every single month and go crazy. So instead, I will hit my goals and any overspending will be paid for through the guardrails I set up in my budget. I will just make up for that overspending my being more intentional with my budget the following months. This makes it clear to me that spending isn’t a free for all! 🤍💻 comment “template” for a link to my budget template!

One cheat day will not ruin all the progress you've made, but multiple cheat days will. So just make sure to keep it in moderation. hook: If you ate this one slice of bread, this is the amount of water that your body would store. By eating just this amount of pasta, your body would store this amount of water.
template: If you (insert verb) this (insert noun) this is the amount of (insert noun) your body would (insert result)
transcript: If you ate this one slice of bread, this is the amount of water that your body would store. By eating just this amount of pasta, your body would store this amount of water. And if you ate this whole pack of rice, then guess what? Your body would store this amount of water. This is about 1kg worth of water. And it seems pretty scary that your body can store all of that just through eating these foods. But carbohydrates act a little bit like a sponge. And the fact that when you eat them, your body also soaks up some water. For every one gram of carbohydrates, typically around three to four grams of water. And this is why when it comes to losing weight, you can't just randomly weigh yourself when you fancy it. Because on the day you catch it down here, you're going to be over the moon. And the day you catch it up here, you're going to hate yourself. This just leads to mixed emotions all the time. And then you self-sabotaging and doing things differently depending on what your weight is in the morning. You have to expect that your weight is going to fluctuate every single day, whether it's by 0.2kg, whether it's by 0.5kg, whether it's by 1kg. But that isn't important. And instead, you need to weigh yourself every morning and take a weekly average. So you compare this weekly average to the next weekly average, to the next one, to the next one. Alongside other measurements of progression, taking progress pictures, doing measurements, going off how your clothes fit, this is going to be the best representation of understanding how much fat you're losing over time. Because remember, you haven't gained a kilo and you haven't lost a kilo overnight. That is close to impossible. So if you are someone that's trying to lose weight and you are weighing yourself, make sure you take this into consideration. And if you want more helpful weight loss content just like this, make sure you drop me a follow.
author: tomhullpt
caption: The majority of foods you eat will retain water when consumed 💧 Some a little, some a lot… depending on the amount of carbohydrates it holds onto That’s why randomly weighing yourself when you fancy it will have you pulling your hair out 😠 You’ve had a really good day… hit your calories, high protein, lots of steps AND a gym session But your weight is 2-3lbs heavier the next morning Then you self sabotage & sack it all off But when it’s down you are over the moon So you need to remove the emotional attachment to daily weighing, and instead focus on weekly averages Weigh every morning, take the average from the week & compare it to the next week Carbs do hold onto 3-4g of water for every 1g after all Don’t spend another day hating yourself because of your weight & take this into consideration instead If that average weight plateaus for 3-4 weeks, then most likely you aren’t in a deficit and need to make changes
